§ 02-17-01 PURPOSE.
   (A)   The purpose of this chapter is to promote the educational, cultural
and economic welfare of the city by engaging in a comprehensive program of
historic preservation to promote, preserve and protect historic buildings,
structures, sites and monuments which serve as visible reminders of the
historical, archeological, architectural, educational and cultural heritage of
the city.
   (B)   It is the further purpose of this chapter to allow for the social and
historical advantages of the city to promote the use and conservation of such
property; to stabilize and improve property values in local historic districts;
to promote the creation of local historic districts; and to encourage new
buildings and developments that will be harmonious with the existing
historical, archeological and architectural structures, sites and monuments.
(Ord. 2905, passed 9-4-2012)
§ 02-17-02 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this chapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   ACCESSORY BUILDING OR STRUCTURE. See §
10-03-11.
   ACQUISITION. The act or process of acquiring fee title or interest other
than fee title of real property (including acquisition of development rights or
remainder interest).
   ADDITION. Any construction that increases the size of an existing building
or structure in terms of site coverage, height, length, width or gross floor
area, including an additional floor.
   ALTERATIONS. Any act or process that changes one or more exterior features
of a building or site or any feature or object on a site.
   BUILDING. For purposes of designation, a resource created principally to
shelter any form of human activity.
   CERTIFICATE OF APPROPRIATENESS. The document issued by the City Historic
Preservation Commission before any buildings, structures or accessory
buildings/structures are erected, altered, restored, moved or demolished within
a local historic district; before any alterations are made to the exterior of
sites or existing structures within a local historic district; before any
changes of use, zoning changes, home occupation permits, special use permits
and/or temporary use permits are allowed within a local historic district.
   CHARACTER DEFINING FACADE. Any elevation that contains features that help to
define a structure’s significance.
   COMMISSION. The Caldwell Historic Preservation Commission.
   CONTRIBUTING. A contributing building, site, structure or object that adds
to the historic architectural qualities, historic associations or archeological
values for which a property is significant because:
      (1)   It was present during the period of significance and possesses
historic integrity reflecting its character at that time or is capable of
yielding important information about the period; or
      (2)   It individually meets the National Register eligibility criteria.
For inventory purposes, PRIMARY shall be used synonymously with CONTRIBUTING.
   COUNCIL. The Caldwell City Council.
   DEMOLITION. Any act or process that permanently, substantially destroys or
razes any building, site, structure or object in whole or in part.
   DEMOLITION BY NEGLECT. Any act or omission that destroys or contributes to
the destruction of a building.
   EXTERIOR FEATURE. The architecture, size, location, type, style, kind,
texture, design, general arrangement and/or material of a building, site,
structure or object, including, but not limited to, windows, doors, exterior
light fixtures, roofs, signs, appurtenant fixtures and fencing, all as visible
from public right-of-way.
   HISTORIC EASEMENT. Any easement, restriction, covenant or condition running
with the land designed and designated to preserve, maintain and enhance all or
part of the existing places of historical, architectural, archeological,
educational or cultural significance.
   HISTORIC LANDMARK. A district, site, building, structure or object that
possesses exceptional significance in history, architecture, engineering,
archeology or culture at the national, state or local level and has been
designated as a historic landmark through the public hearing process outlined
herein and subsequent local ordinance.
   HISTORIC PRESERVATION. The research, protection, restoration and
rehabilitation of buildings, sites, structures, objects or districts
significant in the history, architecture, archeology or culture of the state,
its communities or the nation.
   HISTORIC PROPERTY. Any building, structure, area or site that is significant
in the history, architecture, archeology or culture of this state, its
communities or the nation. A property can be an individual site or a district
consisting of multiple buildings, sites, structures or objects.
   IMPROVEMENT. A valuable addition made to the property (usually real estate)
or amelioration in its condition, amounting to more than mere repairs or
replacement, costing labor or capital, and intended to enhance its value,
beauty or utility or to adapt it for new or further purposes.
   INTEGRITY. The ability of a property to convey its significance; includes
the concepts of location, design, setting, materials, workmanship, feeling and
association.
   LOCAL HISTORIC DISTRICT. Any area designated as such by ordinance which
includes or encompasses such historic buildings, sites, structures or objects
as the Commission may determine to be appropriate for historic preservation.
Such local district or districts need not be a single enclosed area nor do the
areas or sites have to be contiguous to constitute a district. A district may
include contributing, non-contributing or undeveloped properties.
   LOCAL HISTORIC PRESERVATION PLAN. The organization into a logical sequence
of preservation information pertaining to identification, evaluation,
registration and treatment of historic properties and setting priorities for
accomplishing preservation activities, resulting in a written document.
   NATIONAL REGISTER. The National Register of Historic Places. A list
established by the National Historic Preservation Act of 1966 (as amended),
being 54 U.S.C. §§ 300101 et seq. and codified in 36 C.F.R. part 60 (as
amended) of buildings, sites, structures, objects and districts having local,
state or national historical, architectural or cultural significance and
considered worthy of preservation.
   NATIONAL REGISTER CRITERIA. The established criteria for evaluating the
eligibility of properties for inclusion in the National Register of Historic
Places. For further information on the criteria refer to the National Park
Service website, National Register of Historic Places (see http://
www.cr.nps.gov/nr).
   NEW CONSTRUCTION. Construction or installation of an entire structure,
whether primary, secondary or accessory.
   NON-CONTRIBUTING. A building, site, structure or object within a district
may be NON-CONTRIBUTING because: it was not present during the period of
significance; due to alterations, disturbances, additions or other changes, it
no longer possesses historic integrity reflecting its character at that time or
is incapable of yielding important information about the period; or it does not
individually meet the National Register eligibility criteria. A NON-
CONTRIBUTING building, site, structure or object that is within a historic
district remains subject to this chapter. For inventory purposes, SECONDARY
shall be used synonymously with NON-CONTRIBUTING. This classification has been
designated through a survey and a formal hearing process.
   OBJECT. For purposes of designation, a construction primarily artistic in
nature or relatively small in scale and simply constructed, such as a statue or
milepost.
   PERIOD OF SIGNIFICANCE. The length of time when a property was associated
with important events, activities or persons, or attained the characteristics
which qualify it for National Register listing. PERIOD OF SIGNIFICANCE usually
begins with the date when significant activities or events began giving the
property its historic significance; this is often a date of construction.
   PERSON. An individual, firm, corporation, association, municipal corporation
or any other governmental or quasi-governmental agency, or group or combination
thereof acting as a unit, except that nothing in this chapter shall be
construed to allow the designation, regulation, conditioning, restriction or
acquisition of historic buildings, structures, sites or areas or other
properties or facilities owned by the state or any of its political
subdivisions, agencies or instrumentalities.
   PERSON IN CHARGE. The person or persons possessed of the freehold, or a
mortgagee or vendee in possession, assignee of rents, receiver, executor,
trustee, lessee, agent or any person directly or indirectly in control of a
historic property.
   PLANNING DIRECTOR. The Planning and Zoning Director of the city charged with
the administration of the city’s planning and zoning documents, including those
pertaining to historic preservation. This definition includes the Planning
Director’s designated representative(s), also referred to in this chapter as
planning staff.
   PRESERVATION. The act or process of applying measures necessary to sustain
the existing form, integrity and materials of a historic property. Work,
including preliminary measures to protect and stabilize the property, generally
focuses upon the ongoing maintenance and repair of historic materials and
features rather than extensive replacement and new construction. New exterior
additions are not within the scope of this treatment; however, the limited and
sensitive upgrading of mechanical, electrical and plumbing systems and other
code required work to make properties functional is appropriate within a
preservation project. Exterior additions should be sympathetic to the
significant elements of the historic property.
   PRIMARY FACADE. The elevation that most characterizes a structure’s
significance; usually the front elevation.
   PROPERTY. Land and that which is erected or affixed to the land. Real
property extends to rights issuing out of, annexed to and exercisable within or
about land.
   PUBLIC RIGHT-OF-WAY. A portion of land either dedicated or reserved for
public use which normally includes alleys, streets, sidewalks, utilities or
other service functions. For purposes of this chapter, alleys shall not be
included as part of PUBLIC RIGHT-OF-WAY.
   RECONSTRUCTION. The act or process of depicting, by means of new
construction, the form, features and detailing of a non-surviving building,
site, structure or object for the purpose of replicating its appearance at a
specific period of time and in its historic location.
   REHABILITATION. The act or process of making possible a compatible use for a
property through repair, alterations and additions while preserving those
portions of features which convey its historical, cultural or architectural
values.
   RESTORATION. The act or process of accurately depicting the forms, features
and character of a property as it appeared at a particular period of time by
means of the removal of features from other periods in its history and
reconstruction of missing features from the restoration period. The limited and
sensitive upgrading of mechanical, electrical and plumbing systems and other
code required work to make properties functional is appropriate within a
RESTORATION project.
   SECRETARY OF THE INTERIOR’S STANDARDS FOR REHABILITATION. Standards that
were written pursuant to federal law to ensure that work on historic buildings
is done in such a manner which preserves the historical integrity of the
building. For further information refer to the “Secretary of the Interior’s
Standards for the Treatment of Historic Properties with Guidelines for
Preserving, Rehabilitating, Restoring and Reconstructing Historic Buildings.”
   SITE. For purposes of designation, location of a significant event, a
prehistoric or historic occupation or activity, or a building or structure,
whether standing, ruined or vanished, where the location itself possesses
historic, cultural or archeological value regardless of the value of any
existing structures.
   SITE IMPROVEMENTS. A modification to the grounds of a property not including
the buildings or accessory buildings. Such improvements may include, but are
not limited to, fences, walls, greenhouses, storage sheds, outdoor light
fixtures, patios, decks, porches, hot tubs, swimming pools, fountains,
barbecues, outdoor fireplaces, playground equipment, steps or pavement.
   STRUCTURE.
      (1)   For purposes of designation. A functional construction made for
purposes other than creating shelter, such as, but not limited to, a bridge,
canal or dam.
      (2)   For all other purposes. Anything constructed or erected which
requires permanent location on the ground or is attached to something having
location on the ground. STRUCTURES may include, but are not limited to,
buildings, platforms, framework, antennas and prefabricated sheds or other
structures.
   SURVEY FORM. A form that catalogs the age, style, contributing or non-
contributing classification, address, location, photograph, date of inventory,
name of surveyor, building permit history and other relevant information as may
be required by the Planning Director or Commission for a building, site,
structure or object.
   TEMPORARY FEATURES. Items that are erected or displayed for a limited amount
of time, not to exceed 180 days at any one time unless otherwise approved by
the Planning Director, which may include, but are not limited to, sidewalk café
tables, fences, chairs, planters, umbrellas and bicycle racks.
   TEMPORARY STRUCTURES. A structure with or without a foundation that is
erected for a limited amount of time, not to exceed 180 days at any one time
unless otherwise approved by the Planning Director, which may include, but is
not limited to, playhouses and play equipment, mobile buildings and carport/
canopy structures.
(Ord. 2905, passed 9-4-2012)
§ 02-17-03 HISTORIC PRESERVATION COMMISSION.
   (A)   There is hereby created and established a Historic Preservation
Commission which shall consist of no less than five but up to ten members who
shall be appointed by the Mayor with the advice and consent of the Council. In
addition, there shall be one nonvoting liaison member from the Council or city
staff.
   (B)   Members of the Commission shall be appointed with due regard to the
proper representation of such fields as history, architecture, urban planning,
education, archeology and law. Appointed members of the Commission shall live
or work in the city or in the city’s impact area during the full term of
service.
   (C)   The members of the Commission are eligible for reappointment without
regard to the number of terms having been previously served. If a vacancy
occurs, the Mayor with the consent of the Council shall appoint a member to
fill the unexpired term.
   (D)   The members of the Commission shall serve without pay but shall be
reimbursed, with prior permission, by the city for necessary expenses incurred
in connection with their duties.
   (E)   A quorum shall consist of at least 50% or greater of the current
membership and shall not include the nonvoting liaison member from Council or
city staff.
   (F)   The Commission may employ such qualified staff personnel as it deems
necessary.
   (G)   Any member who is absent from four regular meetings in a calendar year
will be notified by letter that the absence limit has been reached. If the
member is subsequently absent from a fifth regular meeting in that same
calendar year, the absence record shall be forwarded to the Mayor for action.
Failure to meet attendance requirements for regular meetings shall be
sufficient grounds for removal from the Commission by action of the City
Council. Members may request a leave of absence for periods of two months to
one year, and upon favorable recommendation by the Commission and approval of
the City Council, each leave may be obtained with no adverse impact upon the
member’s absence record.
   (H)   All members of the Commission shall attend at least one meeting or
training, per year, sponsored by any preservation organization or related
organization. Attendance at Commission meetings does not count toward this
requirement. Failure to meet this requirement shall be sufficient grounds for
removal from the Commission by action of the City Council.
(Ord. 2905, passed 9-4-2012)
§ 02-17-04 PROCEDURES; RULES; MEETINGS; OFFICERS.
   (A)   Rules. The Commission may establish any rules necessary for the
orderly conduct of its business, and all meetings of the Commission shall be
open to the public.
   (B)   Record. The Commission shall keep a record of its attendance,
resolutions, proceedings and actions. The minutes of the preceding Commission
meetings shall be approved by the Commission before any further distribution of
such minutes is made. A copy of the minutes of each meeting shall be kept on
file at the Planning and Zoning Department and City Hall.
   (C)   Regular meetings. Regular meetings shall be scheduled once a month
unless there are not any certificates of appropriateness to review or other
pertinent Commission business to discuss.
   (D)   Special meetings. A special meeting may be called by the Chair of the
Commission whenever he or she deems such meeting necessary. Such special
meeting shall be held at the time and place specified in the call for such a
meeting and each member of the Commission shall be notified of the time and
place of special meetings.
   (E)   Quorum present. In case there shall be no quorum present on the day
fixed for a regular or special meeting, the Commission members present may
adjourn to a specified date and time until a quorum is obtained.
   (F)   Elect officers. At the first meeting of the calendar year, the
appointed Commissioners shall elect officers who shall be Commission members
and who shall serve for terms of one year.
   (G)   Chair. The Chair of the Commission shall preside at all meetings of
the Commission at which he or she is present. He or she shall conduct public
hearings and other public and official meetings held by the Commission. The
Chair shall exercise general guidance and supervision over business and
operation of the Commission and shall present to the Commission such matters
as, in his or her judgment, require the attention of the Commission. The Chair
shall execute all formal documents, including certificates of appropriateness,
on behalf of the Commission and shall, at all times, represent the Commission
in the absence of a duly appointed alternate. The Chair of the Commission shall
vote on all matters and shall have equal privileges as a Commission member
including the right to surrender the Chair for purposes of making motions or
introducing resolutions.
   (H)   Vice Chair. In the absence of the Chair of the Commission, the Vice
Chair of the Commission, or in his or her absence, a Commissioner elected by a
quorum of the Commission shall accede to the duties and obligations of the
office of Chair of the Commission.
   (I)   Planning and zoning staff. Planning and zoning staff shall be
secretary/clerk for the Commission and shall be responsible for swearing in
those who need to testify under oath, taking and keeping minutes and records
for all meetings and hearings, preparing and distributing agendas, keeping
records of properties within local historic districts and all similar items.
   (J)   Committees. The Chair of the Commission shall appoint such committees
as the Commission may direct. He or she may appoint such additional committees
as he or she deems necessary to accomplish the work of the Commission.
(Ord. 2905, passed 9-4-2012; Ord. 3047, passed 3-21-2016; Ord. 3532, passed 9-
5-2023; Ord. 3541, passed 10-17-2023; Ord. 3604, passed 6-18-2024; Ord. 3626,
passed 8-19-2024)
§ 02-17-05 POWERS AND DUTIES OF COMMISSION.
   The Commission shall exercise to the fullest extent the authority granted
under Idaho Code Title 67 (State Government and State Affairs), Chapter 46
(Preservation of Historic Sites) and shall be authorized to:
   (A)   Conduct surveys of local historic properties;
   (B)   Acquire fee and lesser interests in historic properties, including
adjacent or associated lands, by purchase, bequest or donation, but shall not
be authorized to acquire historic properties by condemnation;
   (C)   Preserve, restore, maintain and operate historic properties under the
ownership or control of the Commission;
   (D)   Lease, sell and otherwise transfer or dispose of historic properties
subject to rights of public access and other covenants and in a manner that
will preserve the property;
   (E)   Contract, with the approval of Council, with the state or federal
government, or any agency of either, or with any other organization;
   (F)   Cooperate with the federal, state and local governments in the pursuit
of the objectives of historic preservation;
   (G)   Participate in the conduct of land use, urban renewal and other
planning processes undertaken by the city;
   (H)   Recommend ordinances and otherwise provide information for the
purposes of historic preservation to the Council;
   (I)   Promote and conduct an educational and interpretive program on
historic properties within the jurisdiction of the city;
   (J)   Enter, solely in performance of its official duties and only at
reasonable times, upon private lands for examination or survey thereof.
However, no member, employee or agent of the Commission may enter any private
property, building or structure without the express consent of the owner or
occupant thereof; and
   (K)   Prepare, adopt, maintain and update a local historic preservation plan
for the city.
(Ord. 2905, passed 9-4-2012)
§ 02-17-06 FUNDING.
   (A)   For the purpose of providing funds for a Historic Preservation
Commission, the Council may:
      (1)   Provide funds from current revenues;
      (2)   Receive and expend monies from any other available source or
sources; or
      (3)   Use any combination of divisions (A)(1) or (A)(2) above.
   (B)   Any funds received by the Historic Preservation Commission may be
accumulated from year to year and need not be expended during any one fiscal
year, provided that the maximum accumulation of funds received from ad valorem
taxes shall not exceed twice the amount of money authorized by the Council in
the previous year pursuant to division (A) above.
(Ord. 2905, passed 9-4-2012; Ord. 2923, passed 4-15-2013)
§ 02-17-07 DESIGNATION OF LOCAL HISTORICAL DISTRICTS.
   (A)   Establishment of districts.
      (1)   Generally. The city may establish by ordinance one or more local
historic districts within the area of its jurisdiction. No local historic
district or districts shall be designated until a minimum of one of the
following has been established:
         (a)   Historical or cultural importance;
         (b)   Architectural importance; or
         (c)   Archeological importance, as outlined below.
      (2)   Criteria for designation. The buildings, sites, structures and
objects of a local historic district shall meet one of the following three
criteria:
         (a)   Historical or cultural importance.
            1.   Has significant character, interest or value, as part of the
development, heritage or cultural characteristics of the city, state or nation;
or is associated with the life of a person significant in the past;
            2.   Is the site of a historic event with a significant effect upon
society;
            3.   Exemplifies the cultural, political, economic, social,
educational or historic heritage of the community;
            4.   By being part of or related to a street, square, park or other
distinctive area, should be developed or preserved according to a plan based on
historic, cultural or architectural motif; or
            5.   Owing to its unique location or singular physical
characteristic, represents an established and familiar visual feature of the
neighborhood, community or city.
         (b)   Architectural importance.
            1.   Portrays the environment;
            2.   Embodies those distinguishing characteristics of an
architectural type or engineering specimen;
            3.   Is the work of a designer, architect or craftsman whose
individual work has significantly influenced the development of the city, state
or nation; or
            4.   Contains elements of design, detail, materials or
craftsmanship which represent a significant innovation.
         (c)   Archeological importance.
            1.   Has yielded or may be likely to yield information important in
prehistory or history; or
            2.   Contains or is likely to contain physical remains, such as
relics, monuments, art or symbols, of past human life and activities.
   (B)   Commission research and report on proposed district.
      (1)   The Commission, either by its own initiative or upon the request of
the Council, or upon the request of one or more owners of property in the area
of a proposed local historic district, may recommend the designation of one or
more local historic districts.
      (2)   Prior to recommending designation, the Commission shall make an
investigation of the historical, architectural, archeological and cultural
significance of the buildings, structures, features, sites or surroundings
included in any such proposed local historic district based on the relevant
criteria listed in division (A) above.
      (3)   Thereafter, the Commission shall prepare a report containing
recommendations concerning the area or areas to be included in the proposed
local historic district or districts.
   (C)   Transmittal of report to Planning and Zoning Commission. Copies of the
report shall be transmitted to the City Planning and Zoning Commission for
review and recommendation through the public hearing process as outlined in
Title 10 of this code. Not less than 60 days after the date of transmittal of
such report to the Planning and Zoning Commission, the Historic Preservation
Commission shall hold a public hearing regarding the proposed local historic
district.
   (D)   Notice requirements of the public hearing for Historic Preservation
Commission.
      (1)   Notice of the time, place and purpose of such hearing shall be
given at least 15 calendar days prior to the hearing by one publication in a
newspaper of general circulation in the city; and
      (2)   Written notice of the hearing shall be given to the owners of all
properties, as well as occupants of the properties if different from the
owners, to be included in the local historic district or districts at least 15
calendar days prior to the hearing.
   (E)   Final report to City Council. After conducting the public hearing, the
Commission may vote to proceed with the proposed local historic district, and
shall submit a final report with its recommendations, as well as the
recommendations of the Planning and Zoning Commission, and a draft ordinance to
the City Council.
   (F)   Public hearing by City Council. The City Council shall act on the
report and recommendation in accordance with the public hearing provisions of
Title 10 of this code. Upon approval by the Council of the ordinance
establishing the local historic district, the zoning maps shall be changed to
reflect the addition of the applicable local historic district overlay zone.
   (G)   Notification of district.
      (1)   Upon adoption of the ordinance, the owners of each property within
the local historic district shall be given written notification of said
designation. Occupants of each property, if different from the owners, shall
also be given written notification. Written notifications shall be the
responsibility of the Planning and Zoning Department.
      (2)   The Planning and Zoning Department shall also notify the following
city departments of such designation: Fire Department, Building Department,
Engineering Department and Mapping Department.
      (3)   One copy of the ordinance creating the local historic district
shall be filed in the office of the County Recorder by the City Clerk.
   (H)   Record of local historic districts.
      (1)   The Planning and Zoning Department shall maintain a record of local
historic districts and all properties within local historic districts.
      (2)   All properties within a local historic district may be marked with
a suitable sign or marker on or near the property indicating that the property
has been so designated as part of a local historic district.
   (I)   Investigation or report updates. The physical changes in a local
historic district that are approved by a certificate of appropriateness shall
be added to the record maintained by the Planning and Zoning Department as
identified in division (H) above. Updates to the record are not considered
amendments to the local historic district.
(Ord. 2905, passed 9-4-2012)
§ 02-17-08 DESIGNATION OF HISTORIC LANDMARKS.
   Historic landmarks shall be designated by ordinance and in accordance with
the following requirements.
   (A)   The building, site, structure or object proposed for such designation
may be so designated on the following criteria: historical, architectural,
archeological and cultural significance; suitability for preservation or
restoration; educational value; cost of acquisition, restoration, maintenance,
operation or repair; possibilities for adaptive or alternative use of the
property; appraised value; and the administrative and financial responsibility
of any person or organization willing to underwrite all or a portion of such
costs. In addition, it must meet the criteria established for inclusion in the
National Register of Historic Places.
   (B)   The Commission, either on its own initiative or upon the request of
the City Council, or upon the request of owner of the property proposed to be
designated, may recommend the designation of a historic landmark. Prior to
recommending the designation, the Commission shall conduct studies, research
and investigations based on the relevant criteria listed in division (A) above.
Thereafter, the Commission shall prepare a report containing recommendations
concerning the historic landmark proposed to be designated and a draft of the
designating ordinance to be presented to the City Council for consideration
during a public hearing. The report of the Commission shall include comments
regarding the suitability of the historic landmark for preservation or
restoration.
   (C)   For each designated historic landmark, the designating ordinance shall
require the waiting period prescribed by §
02-17-12 to be observed prior to its demolition, material alteration,
remodeling or removal. The designating ordinance shall also provide guidelines
for a suitable sign or marker on or near the historic landmark indicating that
the property has been so designated.
      (1)   For properties both designated as a historic landmark and located
within a local historic district, the portion of this chapter pertaining to the
districts takes precedence over the waiting period for demolition, material
alteration, remodeling or removal of the structure.
      (2)   For state or federal properties which are designated as historic
landmarks, the designation is an honorary effort, and the city acknowledges
that the repair, maintenance, demolition or remodel of the structure is not
within its jurisdiction.
   (D)   The City Council shall hold a public hearing on the designating
ordinance, after having given written notice to the owners and occupants of the
property and the publication of such notice in the time and manner required by
§
02-17-07.
   (E)   Following such public hearing, the Council may act on the designating
ordinance.
   (F)   Upon passage of the designating ordinance, the owners and occupants of
each designated historic landmark shall be given written notification of said
designation by the Council, and one copy of the designating ordinance shall be
filed in the office of the County Recorder by the City Clerk.
   (G)   The City Clerk shall give notice of such designation to the County Tax
Assessor.
(Ord. 2905, passed 9-4-2012)
§ 02-17-09 CERTIFICATE OF APPROPRIATENESS REQUIRED.
   (A) Alterations and/or new construction in local historic districts.
      (1)   General rules.
         (a)   After the designation by ordinance of a local historic district,
no “exterior feature,” as defined within this chapter, of any building, site,
structure or object, including all appurtenant features, nor aboveground
utility structure nor any type of outdoor advertising sign shall be erected,
altered, restored, moved or demolished within such local historic district
until after an application for a certificate of appropriateness has been
submitted to the Planning and Zoning Department and approved by the Commission.
         (b)   A certificate is required whether or not a building permit is
required, and a certificate of appropriateness must be granted in all cases
before an applicant can obtain any other permit.
         (c)   As part of the application process for a certificate of
appropriateness, the planning staff shall confirm the contributing or non-
contributing classification of the property based upon the survey records.
         (d)   The Commission may delegate to the planning staff review of
certificates of appropriateness that are listed as “staff level” under the
certificate of appropriateness matrix adopted by the Commission and that are in
compliance with the “Secretary of the Interior’s Standards for Rehabilitation
and Guidelines for Rehabilitating Historic Buildings” and the “Steunenberg
Residential Historic District Design Guidelines.”
      (2)   Exceptions. No certificate of appropriateness is required for the
following items:
         (a)   Interior arrangement of any building or structure or any
interior features or fixtures;
         (b)   Temporary structures and features that do not remain in
existence for a time period greater than a total of 45 days in any consecutive
12-month period; and
         (c)   A site or building improvement that does not require a
certificate in the certificate of appropriateness matrix as adopted by
resolution by the Commission and on file in the Planning and Zoning Department.
   (B)   Demolition or relocation in local historic districts. After the
designation by ordinance of a local historic district, no building, site,
structure or object which is a part of such district shall be demolished or
moved until after an application for a certificate of appropriateness relating
to the demolition or moving of such building, site, structure or object has
been submitted to and approved by the Commission through a public hearing. A
certificate of appropriateness will be required whether or not a building
permit is required and a certificate of appropriateness must be granted in all
cases before an applicant can obtain any other permit required for the
demolition or moving of any building, site, structure or object which is part
of a local historic district.
   (C)   Change in zoning classification and/or change in use in designated
local historic districts. Any change in zoning classification as well as any
change in use, preliminary plat, special use, temporary use and/or home
occupation within a local historic district shall first require approval and
issuance of a certificate of appropriateness before an applicant can apply for
or obtain any other permit or license that may be required.
(Ord. 2905, passed 9-4-2012)
§ 02-17-10 APPLICATION REQUIREMENTS; NOTICE; ACTION; APPEAL FOR COMMISSION AND
STAFF LEVEL APPLICATIONS.
   (A)   Application requirements.
      (1)   An application for a certificate of appropriateness shall be
submitted by the owner of the property, or by a representative of such person,
on a form obtained from the Planning and Zoning Department and containing such
information as required by the Commission.
      (2)   The applicant shall be solely responsible for submitting a complete
application in enough time to ensure all required notification deadlines, as
outlined in this chapter, are able to be met.
      (3)   An application seeking demolition or relocation shall provide the
following:
         (a)   A written statement as to why the building, site, structure or
object should be demolished;
         (b)   Photographs of the building, site, structure or object to be
demolished, as well as of adjacent properties; and
         (c)   If applicants wish to be considered for the finding under §
02-17-11-02(D), they shall provide the following additional information:
            1.   Two written reports, prepared, stamped and signed by currently
licensed state design professionals appropriate to the nature of the project,
at least one of which shall be disinterested, stating the structural soundness
of the building or structure proposed for demolition and suitability for reuse;
and
            2.   An analysis of the cost to rehabilitate the existing structure
plus construct the additional square footage and other goals of the
application. These costs shall be completed to include the cost of demolishing
any existing structures and the equivalent new construction and shall be
completed, signed and stamped by a currently licensed state design/contract
professional appropriate to the nature of the project.
   (B)   Public meetings, hearings, notification and action for Commission
level applications.
      (1)   Public meetings; notice. Prior to approval or denial of a
certificate of appropriateness for window, door, roofing, siding replacement
and fencing, except for those certificates of appropriateness approved by staff
level, a public meeting shall be held, notice shall be posted on the premises
not less than seven calendar days prior to the meeting.
      (2)   Hearing; notice. Prior to approval or denial of a certificate of
appropriateness for demolition, relocation, zone change, change of use,
additions, alterations or new construction a public hearing shall be held,
notice shall be posted on the premises not less than seven calendar days prior
to the meeting and notice shall be mailed to the applicant, the property owners
and residents within 300 feet of the exterior boundary of the parcel under
consideration, and to any applicable registered neighborhood associations, a
minimum of 15 days prior to said public hearing.
      (3)   Incomplete application. In the event the Commission receives an
application for review that the Commission deems incomplete or needing
additional information, the request shall be continued to the next meeting.
      (4)   Representative must be present. The property owner(s) or property
owner’s representative shall be present at the meeting for the Commission to
take action on the application.
      (5)   Agenda. The complete agenda for all meetings shall be posted on the
city’s website and in the Development Services Building.
      (6)   Action by the Commission.
         (a)   Approvals. If the Commission determines the proposed request is
appropriate, it shall approve such application with its reasons for the
decision and any applicable conditions of approval and shall issue to the
applicant a certificate of appropriateness.
         (b)   Denials. If the Commission determines that a certificate of
appropriateness should not be issued, it shall place upon its records the
reason for such determination and shall notify the applicant in writing of its
reasons and recommendations, if any, as to what actions could be taken in order
to obtain a certificate.
   (C)   Action and notification for staff level certificates.
      (1)   Within a minimum of ten business days after receipt of an
application, planning staff shall investigate the request and shall either
approve, modify or deny such application.
      (2)   Within five business days of the decision, planning staff shall
notify, in writing, the applicant. Notification shall be deemed complete on the
date notice is provided to the applicant.
   (D)   Appeals.
      (1)   Appeal of Commission level decisions. Any applicant or property
owner or resident within 300 feet of the subject property aggrieved by a
determination of the Commission may appeal to the Council within 15 calendar
days from the date the certificate of appropriateness is approved or denied.
The decision is deemed to have been made on the date the Commission signs the
order of decision. An appeal from the Council may be taken to a court of
competent jurisdiction.
      (2)   Appeal of staff level decisions. A decision of planning staff may
be appealed to the Commission within 15 calendar days from the date the
certificate of appropriateness is approved or denied. The applicant may request
a waiver of the 15-day appeal period for staff level approvals if the request
is made in writing and accompanied by the signatures of all adjacent property
owners and residents indicating that they do not object to the waiver request.
Planning staff shall review all pertinent information and issue a decision on
the request.
   (E)   Term of approval. The term of approval for a certificate of
appropriateness shall be 12 months from the date of signature on the
certificate or may be extended through the issuance of a valid building permit.
The certificate of appropriateness is issued to the property owner and is valid
for both the property and whoever owns the property, within the applicable one-
year time frame. If the property is sold within the one-year time frame, the
certificate of appropriateness shall be transferred from the previous owner to
the new owner. Certificates of appropriateness shall not be transferred from
one property site to another property site but may be transferred between
property owners on and for the same property site.
(Ord. 2905, passed 9-4-2012; Ord. 3126, passed 1-16-2018)
§ 02-17-11 FINDINGS FOR GRANTING A CERTIFICATE OF APPROPRIATENESS.
   (A)   The Commission shall review application(s) with the findings outlined
below as pertaining to the request for a certificate of appropriateness. The
Commission may attach conditions of approval to the application to ensure
compliance with the findings. Modifications to the application may be submitted
and will be considered at a staff level. In reviewing the modification,
planning staff will utilize the original findings under which the application
was reviewed to ensure the project still complies with the requirements for a
certificate of appropriateness.
      (1)   Section
02-17-11-01 (Alterations; Findings);
      (2)   Section
02-17-11-02 (Demolition or Relocation; Findings);
      (3)   Section
02-17-11-03 (Change in Zoning Classification or Change in Use; Findings); and
      (4)   Section
02-17-11-04 (New Construction; Findings).
   (B)   The Commission shall find that the design of the project is consistent
with the following plans and guidelines that apply to the property:
      (1)   “U.S. Secretary of the Interior’s Standards for Rehabilitation and
Guidelines for Rehabilitating Historic Buildings”;
      (2)   
Title 10 of this code, as amended and adopted by City Council;
      (3)   “Steunenberg Residential Historic District Design Guidelines,” as
amended and adopted (copies available in the City Planning and Zoning
Department); and
      (4)   The city comprehensive plan, as amended and adopted by City
Council.
(Ord. 2905, passed 9-4-2012; Ord. 3126, passed 1-16-2018)
§ 02-17-11-01 ALTERATIONS; FINDINGS.
   The Commission’s decision in regard to certificates of appropriateness for
alterations shall be based on the following findings as applicable to that
property or request and as they relate to historic preservation.
   (A)   The request is consistent with the “Steunenberg Residential Historic
District Design Guidelines.”
   (B)   The request is consistent with the “Secretary of the Interior’s
Standards for Rehabilitation and Guidelines for Rehabilitating Historic
Buildings.”
   (C)   The request supports the goals, policies and recommendations of the
city’s comprehensive plan and the plans referenced therein.
   (D)   Based on the adopted design guidelines the request will not be
incongruous with the historical, architectural, archeological, educational or
cultural aspects of the local district.
   (E)   The request complies with the dimensional standards and other
applicable requirements of
Title 10 of this code, including, but not limited to, setbacks, height
restrictions and parking requirements, unless the Commission finds that
modifying those standards is necessary to protect the overall characteristics
of the local district and to comply with the adopted design guidelines.
(Ord. 2905, passed 9-4-2012)
§ 02-17-11-02 DEMOLITION OR RELOCATION; FINDINGS.
   In order for the Commission to approve a demolition or relocation request,
at least three out of the following five findings must be met:
   (A)   The building, site, structure or object is not classified as
contributing within the local district as stated on the survey form on file in
the Planning and Zoning Department;
   (B)   The building, site, structure or object cannot reasonably meet
national, state or local criteria for designation as a historic property;
   (C)   The demolition of the building, site, structure or object would not
have an adverse impact on the character of the district and/or the adjacent
properties and/or would not put the district at risk of losing historical
status;
   (D)   The owner has reasonably demonstrated that rehabilitation of the
building, site, structure or object would not be economically practical,
realistic or viable based on review of the information required in §
02-17-10(A)(3)(c); and
   (E)   Plans have been submitted to redevelop the property if the demolition
proceeds and such plans will have a positive effect on the district and/or
adjacent properties. The size, scale, use, materials and/or overall design of
the project may be considered as qualities for producing a positive effect.
(Ord. 2905, passed 9-4-2012)
§ 02-17-11-03 CHANGE IN ZONING CLASSIFICATION OR CHANGE IN USE; FINDINGS.
   The Commission’s decision in regard to certificates of appropriateness for a
change in zoning classification, change in use, home occupation permit, special
use permit and/or temporary use permit shall be based on the following
findings:
   (A)   The request supports the city’s comprehensive plan goals, policies and
recommendations contained within § 11 (Special Sites/Historic Areas) of said
plan;
   (B)   The request will be congruous with the historical, architectural,
archeological, educational or cultural significance of the local district; and
   (C)   There will be no significant effect on the exterior of the site.
(Ord. 2905, passed 9-4-2012)
§ 02-17-11-04 NEW CONSTRUCTION; FINDINGS.
   The following objectives and findings, in addition to those cited under §
02-17-11-01, shall be considered where applicable to the proposal.
   (A)   Minimizes traffic impact. The site design minimizes impact of traffic
on adjacent streets and that the pedestrian and bicyclist have been provided
for by requiring sidewalks, landscaping and safe parking lot design as
appropriate.
   (B)   Landscaping.
      (1)   The proposed landscaping enhances the historic district and
neighborhood with attributes that include, but are not limited to, protection
of desirable existing trees, provision of street trees and adequate screening
methods where needed to buffer adjacent uses and unsightly areas or features.
      (2)   Considerations relative to this division (B):
         (a)   The location, height and materials of walls, fences, hedges and
screening plantings to ensure harmony with adjacent developments;
         (b)   The planting of street trees and the unnecessary destruction of
existing trees and landscape features; and
         (c)   The provision of plantings or other screening methods reasonably
required to conceal outdoor storage areas, trash receptacles, exposed machinery
installation, utility buildings and installations and similar accessory areas
or other unsightly developments.
   (C)   On-site grading and drainage. On-site grading and drainage have been
designed so as to minimize off-site impact and provide for erosion control as
required by the city.
   (D)   Review of building mass. The mass of the building shall be reviewed
for its relationship to other buildings within the local historic district.
   (E)   Proportion of building facades. The height to width relationship shall
be compatible and consistent with the predominant architectural character of
the local historic district.
   (F)   Shadow relief/design interest. The exterior of the building shall
provide shadow relief and design interest compatible with the architectural
character of the local historic district.
   (G)   Appropriateness of materials. The appropriateness of materials shall
be reviewed as they relate to building mass, shadow relief and compatibility
with other buildings within the local historic district.
   (H)   Consistency of design. The Commission shall find that the design of
the project is consistent with the plans and guidelines listed in §
02-17-11.
(Ord. 2905, passed 9-4-2012)
§ 02-17-12 PROCEDURE FOR DEMOLITION OR CHANGE IN USE OF HISTORIC LANDMARK.
   (A)   A historic landmark so designated by ordinance, which is not part of a
local historic district, may be demolished, materially altered, remodeled,
relocated or put to a different use only after 180 days’ written notice of the
owner’s proposed action has been given to the Commission in accordance with the
following procedures.
      (1)   During this period, the Commission may negotiate with the owner and
with any other parties in an effort to find a means of preserving the property.
      (2)   During this period, or at any time prior thereto following notice
of designation to the owner, and where such action is reasonably necessary or
appropriate for the continued preservation of the property, the Commission may
enter into negotiations with the owner for the acquisition by gift, purchase or
exchange of the property or any interest therein.
   (B)   The Commission may reduce the waiting period required by this section
in any case where the owner would suffer extreme hardship, unless a reduction
in the required period was allowed. The Commission shall have the discretionary
authority to waive all or any portion of the required waiting period, provided
that the alteration, remodeling, relocation or change of use is undertaken
subject to conditions agreed to by the Commission ensuring the continued
maintenance of the historical, architectural, archeological or cultural
integrity and character of the property.
   (C)   At the end of the required waiting period, as reduced or waived if
such is the case, the designation of such historic landmark shall be rescinded
as necessary and a draft of a proposed ordinance removing such designation
shall be prepared and submitted to the Council for approval.
(Ord. 2905, passed 9-4-2012)
§ 02-17-13 ORDINARY REPAIRS; PUBLIC SAFETY.
   (A)   Nothing in this chapter shall be construed to prevent the ordinary
maintenance or repair of any exterior feature in a local historic district, or
of any historic landmark, which does not involve a change in design, material
or outer appearance thereof, nor to prevent the construction, reconstruction,
alteration, restoration or demolition of any such feature when the Building
Official shall certify such is required for the public safety because of an
unsafe or dangerous condition.
   (B)   (1)   Neither the owner nor the person in charge of a designated
historic landmark or property within a local historic district shall permit it
to fall into a state of disrepair which may result in the deterioration of any
exterior appurtenance or architectural feature so as to produce or tend to
produce, in the judgment of the Commission, a detrimental effect upon its
historic character, including, but not limited to, the deterioration of
exterior walls or other vertical supports; the deterioration of the foundation;
the deterioration of exterior chimneys; the deterioration of roofs or other
horizontal members; the deterioration or removal of exterior finishes or
fenestration; the ineffective waterproofing of exterior walls, roofs and
foundations including broken windows or doors; and/or the deterioration of any
feature so as to create or permit the creation of any hazardous or unsafe
condition or conditions.
      (2)   If the Commission makes a preliminary determination that a property
is being demolished by neglect as described in this division (B), it shall
direct planning and zoning code enforcement to notify the owner(s) of the
property of this preliminary determination, stating the reasons therefor and
the actions necessary, and shall give the owner of record 28 days from the date
of mailing of such notice to submit a plan and a time frame to correct the
specific defects as determined by the Commission.
(Ord. 2905, passed 9-4-2012)
§ 02-17-14 ACQUISITION OF PROPERTY.
   (A)   All lands, buildings, structures, sites or areas acquired by funds
appropriated by the city shall be acquired in the name of the city unless
otherwise provided by the governing board. So long as owned by the city,
historic properties may be maintained by or under the supervision and control
of the city.
   (B)   Nothing in this chapter shall be construed to allow the designation,
regulation, conditioning, restriction or acquisition of historic buildings,
structures, sites or areas, or other properties or facilities owned by the
state or any of its political subdivisions, agencies or instrumentalities.
(Ord. 2905, passed 9-4-2012)
§ 02-17-15 ACQUISITION OF HISTORIC EASEMENTS.
   (A)   The city may acquire, by purchase or donation, historic easements in
any area within the jurisdiction of the city wherever and to the extent the
Council determines that the acquisition will be in the public interest.
   (B)   The Council shall seek a recommendation from the Commission regarding
the historic easement and proposed resolution.
(Ord. 2905, passed 9-4-2012)
§ 02-17-16 EXEMPTION FROM FIRE OR BUILDING CODES.
   The Council, in order to promote the preservation and restoration of any
historic landmark/property, or property within a local historic district may,
upon recommendation of the Commission, exempt a historic landmark or property
within a local historic district from the application of the city fire or
building codes upon compliance with the criteria for exemption set forth in
said codes, and provided the city has adopted such codes, and upon a finding
that non-exemption would prevent or seriously hinder the preservation or
restoration of said historic landmark or property in a local historic district.
(Ord. 2905, passed 9-4-2012)
§ 02-17-17 PENALTIES; REMEDIES.
   Any person or corporation, whether owner, lessee, principal agent, employee
or otherwise, violating any portion of this chapter or permitting any such
violation or failing to comply with any of the requirements contained within
this chapter shall be guilty of a misdemeanor punishable by a fine not
exceeding $300. Each day that a violation continues to exist may constitute a
separate offense. The availability of criminal prosecution of violators of this
chapter shall in no way limit the other remedies that may be available to the
city to enforce the provisions of this chapter, whether in law or in equity,
including injunctive relief.
(Ord. 2905, passed 9-4-2012)
CHAPTER 19: CITY TRAFFIC COMMISSION
Section
   
02-19-01   Commission created
   
02-19-03   Membership; terms of office
   
02-19-05   Organization
   
02-19-07   Duties
§ 02-19-01 COMMISSION CREATED.
   There is hereby created and established a Commission to be known as the City
Traffic Commission.
(Ord. 2861, passed 2-22-2011)
§ 02-19-03 MEMBERSHIP; TERMS OF OFFICE.
   (A)   Membership. The City Traffic Commission shall consist of the Public
Works Director, the City Engineer, the Chief of Police, the Fire Chief, the
Planning and Zoning Director, the Street Superintendent, or their designees,
and one at large member.
   (B)   Terms of office. The at large member shall be appointed for a term of
three years commencing January 1 and ending on December 31 by the Mayor and
City Council. Any vacancy shall be filled by appointment in the same manner and
shall serve only for the remainder of the term which is vacant.
(Ord. 2861, passed 2-22-2011)
§ 02-19-05 ORGANIZATION.
   (A)   The Commission shall meet quarterly (four times per year). Additional
meetings may be called for by the Public Works Director, as necessary.
   (B)   The Public Works Director shall serve as Chair of the Commission, and
the Chief of Police shall serve as the Vice Chair of the Commission. The Chair
shall preside at meetings of the Commission. The Vice Chair shall, in the
absence of the Chair, perform the duties of the Chair.
   (C)   All meetings of the Commission shall be open to the public and follow
the requirements of the state’s open meeting laws (see Idaho Code Title 67,
Chapter 23). The Commission shall keep minutes and other appropriate written
records. A simple majority of Commission members present at any given meeting
constitutes a quorum.
(Ord. 2861, passed 2-22-2011; Ord. 3405, passed 3-21-2022)
§ 02-19-07 DUTIES.
   The Commission is formed for the purpose of making recommendations to the
Mayor and City Council in all matters pertaining to traffic safety.
(Ord. 2861, passed 2-22-2011)
CHAPTER 21: TRUSTEES OF THE CITY EMPLOYEE BENEFIT PLAN TRUST AGREEMENT
Section
   
02-21-01   Appointment; provisions of trust agreement on file
§ 02-21-01 APPOINTMENT; PROVISIONS OF TRUST AGREEMENT ON FILE.
   This section codifies, ratifies and recognizes the appointment of Trustees
pursuant to the City Employee Benefit Plan Trust Agreement (referred to
hereinafter in this section as “trust agreement”), executed on or about
September 2, 2008. The purpose of said document, in part, and by its own stated
terms, is “to provide for the payment of eligible expenses incurred by plan
participants for certain services.” The trust agreement appoints as the initial
Trustees: the Human Resources Director for the city; and the Finance Director/
Treasurer for the city. It further provides that the Trustees shall be allowed
to appoint ex officio members or administrative staff as needed, upon
notification to City Council. The trust agreement further contains provisions
relating to the term of each Trustee, the processes for resignation or removal
and for the appointment of successor Trustees, notice for and meetings of
Trustees, voting, powers, recordkeeping, liability and providing for the
promulgation of rules and regulations pertaining to the sound and efficient
administration of the trust agreement. A copy of the trust agreement, as it may
be amended from time to time, and information relating to the identity of
currently serving Trustees shall be available to the public upon request made
to the City Clerk.
(Ord. 2940, passed 7-1-2013)
CHAPTER 25: AUDIT COMMITTEE
Section
   
02-25-01   Creation; composition
   
02-25-03   Meetings
   
02-25-05   Authority and responsibility
   
02-25-07   Audit Committee bylaws
§ 02-25-01 CREATION; COMPOSITION.
   (A)   Creation. The Council hereby constitutes and establishes an Audit
Committee.
   (B)   Composition. The Committee shall be comprised of five members
appointed by the Council, two of whom are members of the Council Finance
Committee, and three (the independent members) who are independent of
management and the independent auditor. The independent members’ terms shall be
three years and staggered so that the Committee annually includes a new
independent member and independent members with one and two years’ service. One
independent member shall be appointed Chairperson by the Council.
(Ord. 1898, passed 5-6-1991)
§ 02-25-03 MEETINGS.
   (A)   Meeting times. The Audit Committee is to meet at least two times per
year unless additional meeting(s) are necessary, as determine by the Finance
Director.
   (B)   Attendance. Members of the Audit Committee are to be present at all
meetings. As necessary or desirable, the Chairperson may request that members
of management, the Director of Internal Audit and representatives of the
independent auditor be present at a meeting of the Committee.
   (C)   Minutes. Minutes of each meeting are to be prepared and approved by
the Committee members and provided to the Council. Approved minutes are to be
available for public inspection.
(Ord. 1898, passed 5-6-1991; Ord. 3405, passed 3-21-2022)
§ 02-25-05 AUTHORITY AND RESPONSIBILITY.
   The Audit Committee is to serve as a focal point for communication between
the Council, the independent auditor, internal auditor and management, as their
duties relate to financial accounting, reporting and internal controls and
compliance. The Audit Committee is to assist the Council in fulfilling its
responsibilities as to accounting policies and reporting practices of the city
and sufficiency of auditing relative thereto. It is to be the Council’s
principal agent in assuring the independence of the city’s independent
auditors, the integrity of management and the adequacy of disclosures to the
public. However, the opportunity for the independent auditors to meet with the
entire Council as needed is not to be restricted. The Committee shall oversee
and advise the Council and management on the selection of independent auditors.
(Ord. 1898, passed 5-6-1991)
§ 02-25-07 AUDIT COMMITTEE BYLAWS.
   The Committee’s operational guidelines are set down in the Audit Committee
bylaws and may be amended, after consultation with the Council, by a majority
vote of the independent members. The authority and responsibility of the Audit
Committee and the appointment and terms of members are designated in the bylaws
and are incorporated herein by reference.
(Ord. 1898, passed 5-6-1991)
CHAPTER 27: CITY EXECUTIVE AIRPORT ADVISORY BOARD
Section
   
02-27-01   Creation and composition
   
02-27-03   Membership; appointment; terms; and vacancies
   
02-27-05   Duties and responsibilities
   
02-27-07   Meetings
   
02-27-09   Officers
   
02-27-11   Records
§ 02-27-01 CREATION AND COMPOSITION.
   (A)   An Airport Advisory Board is hereby created, consisting of not less
than three nor more than seven voting members, all of whom shall be appointed
by the Mayor and approved by a majority vote of the City Council. The members
of the Board shall serve without compensation. The term of office for each
member shall be for a period of three years. The Board shall elect a
Chairperson and Vice Chairperson. The Chairperson shall preside and direct all
Board meetings. In the absence of the Chairperson, the Vice Chairperson shall
preside and direct the meeting.
   (B)   The City Director of Aviation, or his or her designee, shall serve in
a non-voting capacity as a facilitator at Board meetings. The facilitator is
responsible for assisting the Chairperson in the process of the meeting(s).
(Ord. 3540, passed 10-3-2023; Ord. 3540-A, passed 11-21-2023)
§ 02-27-03 MEMBERSHIP; APPOINTMENT; TERMS; AND VACANCIES.
   (A)   Membership. The membership of the Advisory Board shall be composed of:
      (1)   At least one, but not more than three, members that are general
aviation users that do not affiliate with a commercial entity at the Caldwell
Executive Airport. A minimum of one of these members shall be a resident of the
city or live within the city impact area;
      (2)   At least one, but not more than three, members that are owner/
operators of a commercial entity at the Caldwell Executive Airport. A minimum
of one of these members shall be a resident of the city or live within the city
impact area;
      (3)   One member shall also be a member of the City Council, assigned to
the Board;
      (4)   The Board is encouraged to involve young aviators and may have one
additional non-voting member who is a city resident under the age of 18; and
      (5)   Staggered terms should be implemented to ensure that no more than
three Board member terms expire in any given year. No member shall serve more
than three full consecutive terms.
   (B)   Attendance. Board members are expected to attend as many meetings as
possible. Missing multiple meetings throughout the calendar year or missing two
or more consecutive meetings without prior consent from the Chairperson shall
be grounds for being removed from the Board by the City Council.
   (C)   Removal. Removal of any Board member(s) shall take place as stated in
Title 2, Chapter 6.
   (D)   Youth member. The youth member shall be appointed to a term of up to
one year and may be reappointed for up to two successive terms not to exceed a
sitting time of three years.
(Ord. 3540, passed 10-3-2023; Ord. 3540-A, passed 11-21-2023)
§ 02-27-05 DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES.
   It shall be the duty of the Board to provide recommendations to the city
based on the airport’s needs based on an analysis of how they can assist the
city in implementing FAA-approved master plan and grant assurance projects to
assist in the orderly and efficient administration and operation of the
Caldwell Executive Airport. This may include:
   (A)   To study the economic and physical conditions and problems in
connection with the maintenance, operation, regulation, control and use of
Caldwell Executive Airport;
   (B)   To propose recommendations for the operation, control and use of
Caldwell Executive Airport, and the maintenance and operation of hangars,
repair shops, depots, taxi strips and all other facilities and utilities
required, necessary or convenient for the proper orderly and efficient
administration, operation, superintendence and control of the Caldwell
Executive Airport;
   (C)   To propose recommendations and suggestions for the purpose of planning
for further growth, development and regulation of the Caldwell Executive
Airport in order to promote the public interest, convenience and welfare in the
administration and operation of the Caldwell Executive Airport, as well as to
promote business activities to serve as a catalyst for economic development
throughout the city and region;
   (D)   All proposals for changes to current airport rules and regulations and
minimum standards proposed by the Board will be reviewed by the Board
facilitator, Chairperson and Vice Chairperson to ensure FAA compliance.
Reviewed proposals shall be submitted to City Council for approval and
ratification and, after such approval and ratification, shall have the force
and effect of ordinance;
   (E)   To advise the City Aviation Administration regarding rules and
regulations for aircraft traffic regulation, airport facilities and runway
improvements; and
   (F)   To formulate, propose and recommend such rules and regulations as are
necessary or desirable to carry out the intent and purpose of this chapter.
(Ord. 3540, passed 10-3-2023; Ord. 3540-A, passed 11-21-2023)
§ 02-27-07 MEETINGS.
   The Board shall meet on a regular basis, no less than once per quarter.
Additional meetings may be called by the Chairperson, city staff or at the
request of the Mayor upon a minimum of seven calendar days’ written notice to
all members of the Board. The facilitator, in conjunction with the Chairperson,
shall prepare the agenda for each meeting. Complete minutes shall be kept by
the Secretary of the Board. Unless otherwise noticed, all Board meetings shall
take place at Hubler Terminal at the Caldwell Executive Airport.
(Ord. 3540, passed 10-3-2023; Ord. 3540-A, passed 11-21-2023)
§ 02-27-09 OFFICERS.
   (A)   Chairperson. The Chairperson is responsible for the meeting’s outcomes
and work product.
   (B)   Vice Chairperson. The Vice Chairperson stands in for the Chair in his
or her absence.
   (C)   Secretary. The Director of Aviation, or his or her designee, shall act
as Secretary for all meetings. He or she shall be responsible for keeping
minutes of each meeting and shall provide said minutes to the facilitator after
each meeting for them to be distributed to the Board.
   (D)   Election. The Board shall elect a Chairperson and Vice Chairperson
from current voting Board members, excluding the City Council member.
(Ord. 3540, passed 10-3-2023; Ord. 3540-A, passed 11-21-2023)
§ 02-27-11 RECORDS.
   The Recorder (Board facilitator) shall take written or media record of
meeting proceedings and produce official minutes of said record within five
business days from meeting completion showing the discussion topics and outcome
of each meeting and other official actions.
(Ord. 3540, passed 10-3-2023)

CHAPTER 32: PARKS AND RECREATION COMMISSION
Section
   
02-32-01   Commission created
   
02-32-02   Membership
   
02-32-03   Terms of office
   
02-32-04   Organization
   
02-32-05   Powers; duties
§ 02-32-01 COMMISSION CREATED.
   There is hereby created and established a Commission to be known as the City
Parks and Recreation Commission.
(Ord. 3508, passed 6-6-2023)
§ 02-32-02 MEMBERSHIP.
   The City Parks and Recreation Commission shall consist of not less than
three nor more than seven voting members, including one member of the City
Council. An appointed member of the Commission must reside in the city and must
remain a resident of the city during service on the Commission. All members
shall be appointed by the Mayor and confirmed by majority vote of the City
Council. Appointment of one youth advisory member is welcome and encouraged,
with the term of office expiring on August 31 of each year.
(Ord. 3508, passed 6-6-2023)
§ 02-32-03 TERMS OF OFFICE.
   The term of office for members shall not be more or less than three years,
provided however, that at the expiration of said term of office, the member
shall be eligible for two additional consecutive reappointments, each for one
full term in addition to the original term already served. No person shall
serve more than two full consecutive terms without specific concurrence by two-
thirds of the Council adopted by motion and recorded in the minutes. In no case
shall any person serve more than three full consecutive terms. Vacancies
occurring otherwise than through the expiration of terms shall be filled in the
same manner as the original appointment. Members may be removed pursuant to
Title 2, Chapter 6.
(Ord. 3508, passed 6-6-2023)
§ 02-32-04 ORGANIZATION.
   (A)   The Commission shall meet monthly, with an exception being made should
a meeting for that month be unnecessary. Additional meetings may be called for
by the Parks and Recreation Director, as necessary. The Commission shall elect
a Chairperson and create and fill any other office it may deem necessary. The
Chairperson shall preside at meetings of the Commission. The Vice Chairperson
shall, in the absence of the Chairperson, perform the duties of the
Chairperson. All meetings of the Commission shall be open to the public and
follow the requirements of the state’s open meeting laws. Executive sessions
may be closed by the presiding officer pursuant to Idaho Code § 74-206.
   (B)   A member of the city’s parks and recreation staff shall keep minutes
and other appropriate written records on behalf of the Commission. A simple
majority of Commission members present at any given meeting constitutes a
quorum.
(Ord. 3508, passed 6-6-2023)
§ 02-32-05 POWERS; DUTIES.
   It shall be the duty of the Commission to recommend and make suggestions to
the Council regarding:
   (A)   The formation of new parks and acquisition of land;
   (B)   The development of new pathways;
   (C)   The renovation and expansion of current city parks; and
   (D)   The implementation or updating of park policies and recreation
programming.
(Ord. 3508, passed 6-6-2023)
CHAPTER 33: INDUSTRIAL DEVELOPMENT CORPORATION
Section

§ 02-33-01 PURPOSE.
   The industrial development corporation was created by the city pursuant to
Idaho Code Title 50, Chapter 27 (the “Act”), for the purposes set forth in the
Act, to promote employment, encourage the development of new jobs, maintain and
supplement the capital investments in industry that currently exist in the
city, encourage future employment by ensuring future capital investment,
attract environmentally sound industry, protect and enhance the quality of
natural resources and the environment and to promote the products and
conservation of energy.
(Ord. 2899, passed 2-21-2012)
§ 02-33-03 AUTHORITY.
   The powers and authority of the industrial development corporation are
provided in the state code, including, but not limited to, those powers set
forth in Idaho Code § 50-2708 and the remainder of the Act, as amended, to the
extent said powers are not limited by Ord. 1633 of the city or by the
industrial development corporation’s charter, bylaws and/or rules and
regulations.
(Ord. 2899, passed 2-21-2012)
