CHAPTER 37: DESIGN REVIEW COMMISSION
Section
   
02-37-01   Commission created
   
02-37-02   Appointment; term
   
02-37-03   Organization
   
02-37-04   Meetings
   
02-37-05   Powers, duties and responsibilities
§ 02-37-01 COMMISSION CREATED.
   There shall be a Design Review Commission for the city, which shall be known
and designated as the “Design Review Commission” (DRC).
(Ord. 3083, passed 4-17-2017)
§ 02-37-02 APPOINTMENT; TERM.
   (A)   The DRC shall consist of at least three and no more than seven
Commissioners, all of whom shall be appointed by the Mayor with the consent of
the City Council. Appointed members of the Commissions shall live or work in
the city or in the city’s impact area during the full term of service.
Commissioners shall have a background and interest in community design such as
architects, planners, engineers, builders, developers, historians, business
persons and property owners.
   (B)   When a vacancy occurs for any reason other than an expired term a new
Commissioner shall be appointed to complete the remainder of that term.
Commissioners shall be appointed to two- and three-year terms that are equally
staggered. Subsequent terms shall be three years in length for all
Commissioners.
(Ord. 3083, passed 4-17-2017; Ord. 3627, passed 8-19-2024)
§ 02-37-03 ORGANIZATION.
   The DRC shall elect its own Chair and Vice Chair. Election of officers shall
take place annually during the first meeting of the calendar year. During the
absence of the Chair, the Vice Chair shall assume the duties of the Chair. The
Planning and Zoning Director, or a designated representative, shall serve as
secretary and shall store recordings and produce accurate minutes of all
Commission meetings.
(Ord. 3083, passed 4-17-2017)
§ 02-37-04 MEETINGS.
   The DRC shall hold meetings on an as needed basis. The DRC shall decide on
the date and time of the meeting. Regular meetings shall at all times be open
to the public.
(Ord. 3083, passed 4-17-2017; Ord. 3542, passed 10-17-2023)
§ 02-37-05 POWERS, DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES.
   (A)   The DRC shall review projects requested by the applicant for
compliance with design review standards within §§ 10-12-05 (City Center Design
Requirements) and 10-12-06 (City Center Indian Creek Corridor Design
Requirements).
   (B)   The DRC’s jurisdiction is limited to new construction, building
additions or exterior renovations on properties in the City Center Zoning
District as determined on the official zoning map for the city.
   (C)   The DRC shall review projects and either approve, approve with
conditions or deny such application. The Planning and Zoning Director, or a
designated representative, shall then notify the applicant in writing of the
decision.
   (D)   Staff decisions may be appealed to the DRC, and, conversely, DRC
decisions may be appealed to the City Council for review and decision. Appeals
shall be filed in accordance will all city ordinances.
   (E)   The powers, duties and responsibilities of the DRC shall comply with
the State Local Land Use Planning Act of 1975, being Idaho Code Title 67,
Chapter 65.
(Ord. 3083, passed 4-17-2017)
CHAPTER 38: DOWNTOWN PARKING ADVISORY BOARD
Section
   
02-38-01   Commission created
   
02-38-02   Duties and responsibilities of the Board
   
02-38-03   Meetings
§ 02-38-01 COMMISSION CREATED.
   (A)   Creation. There is hereby created and established a Downtown Parking
Advisory Board which shall consist of not less than three and no more than
seven voting Board members.
   (B)   Expiration. The Advisory Board shall be active and perform the duties
as specified in this chapter for a period of two years from the effective date
of this chapter. The Board will sunset on February 18, 2027, unless
reestablished or extended by formal action of the City Council.
   (C)   Voting members. All voting members shall be appointed by the Mayor and
confirmed by a majority vote of the City Council. Appointed members of the
Board shall meet at least one of the following criteria:
      (1)   A citizen of the city with his or her main residence located within
city limits;
      (2)   Be the owner of real property located within the Downtown Business
District; or
      (3)   Be the owner of an active business within the Downtown Business
District. An owner of property shall mean the title holder, purchaser under a
contract for deed, lessee.
   (D)   Non-voting members. In addition, the Mayor shall assign a City Council
member to sit on the Board as a non-voting Council liaison. The City Community
Development Director, or his or her designee, shall serve in a non-voting
capacity as a facilitator at Board meetings. The facilitator is responsible for
assisting the Chairperson in the process of the meeting(s).
   (E)   Members; initial term. All Board members shall be appointed for an
initial two-year term. After two years, if the City Council votes for the
Advisory Board to continue and remain active in its duties, existing Board
member terms may be extended, or new Board members may be appointed.
   (F)   Compensation. The members of the Board shall serve without
compensation.
   (G)   Vacancies. Vacancies occurring otherwise than through the expiration
of terms shall be filled in the same manner as the original appointment.
(Ord. 3657, passed 2-18-2025)
§ 02-38-02 DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF THE BOARD.
   The Downtown Parking Advisory Board will advise and make policy
recommendations to city staff and City Council on all aspects of public parking
within the city’s downtown districts. The purpose of the Board is to provide
citizen and property owner input into the policy decisions for the city related
to all aspects of public parking, including, but not limited to, on-street
parking, parking lots and parking fees.
(Ord. 3657, passed 2-18-2025)
§ 02-38-03 MEETINGS.
   (A)   Regular meetings. Regular meetings shall be scheduled no less than
once a quarter. Regular meetings shall at all times be open to the public.
   (B)   Special meetings. Special meetings may be called by the Chairperson,
city staff or at the request of the Mayor upon a minimum of five calendar days’
written notice to all members of the Board.
   (C)   Record. The facilitator, in conjunction with the Chairperson, shall
keep a record of its attendance, proceedings and actions, and prepare the
agenda for each meeting. Complete minutes shall be kept by the facilitator of
the Board, or his or her designee.
   (D)   Quorum present. In case there shall be no quorum present on the day
fixed for a regular or special meeting, the Commission members present may
adjourn to a specified date and time until a quorum is obtained.
   (E)   Attendance. Board members are expected to attend as many meetings as
possible. Missing multiple meetings throughout the calendar year or missing two
or more consecutive meetings without prior consent from the Chairperson shall
be grounds for being removed from the Board by the City Council.
   (F)   Removal. Removal of any Board member(s) shall take place as stated in
Title 2, Chapter 6.
   (G)   Election of officers. The Board shall elect its own Chair and Vice
Chair. Election of officers shall take place annually during the first meeting
of the calendar year. During the absence of the Chair, the Vice Chair shall
assume the duties of the Chair.
   (H)   Chairperson. The Chairperson shall preside over and direct all
meetings of the Board. The Chairperson shall be responsible for ensuring that
all meetings are conducted in an orderly and effective manner.
   (I)   Vice Chairperson. In the absence of the Chairperson, the Vice
Chairperson shall assume the duties of the Chairperson.
(Ord. 3657, passed 2-18-2025)

CHAPTER 1: GENERAL PROVISIONS
Section
   
03-01-01   Officers to take oath of office
   
03-01-03   Bonds of certain city officers
   
03-01-05   Mayor and Council salaries
§ 03-01-01 OFFICERS TO TAKE OATH OF OFFICE.
   The various officers of the city shall take and subscribe before some
officer authorized to administer oaths such oath as is required by law of
municipal officers (see Idaho Code § 59-401), which oath shall be filed with
the Clerk. No officer shall enter upon the performance of the duties of his or
her office until he or she shall have subscribed and filed such oath as
required herein.
(Ord. 913, passed 7-6-1962)
§ 03-01-03 BONDS OF CERTAIN CITY OFFICERS.
   (A)   The Clerk, Treasurer, Finance Director and Chief of Police, before
entering upon the duties of their offices, shall file with the Clerk good and
sufficient bonds with responsible sureties, in amounts as may be determined and
approved by the Council, conditioned upon the faithful performance of the
duties of their respective offices.
   (B)   All other employees of the city whose duties involve the handling of
monies shall be covered by blanket bond in amounts as may be determined and
approved by the City Council.
(Ord. 913, passed 7-6-1962; Ord. 3447, passed 8-18-2022)
§ 03-01-05 MAYOR AND COUNCIL SALARIES.
   (A)   Elected officials.
      (1)   Mayor. The annual salary of the Mayor shall be as follows:
         (a)   Commencing January 1, 2024, the Mayor shall receive a biweekly
salary in the sum of $3,752.
         (b)   Commencing January 1, 2026, the Mayor shall receive a biweekly
salary in the sum of $3,940.
      (2)   Council. The annual salary of each member of the City Council shall
be as follows:
         (a)   Commencing January 1, 2024, each member of the City Council
shall receive a biweekly salary in the sum of $451.
         (b)   Commencing January 1, 2026, each member of the City Council
shall receive a biweekly salary in the sum of $474.
   (B)   Appointive officers. All officers and employees of the city, other
than elected officials, shall be paid salaries or fees in such amounts as may
be set from time to time by the City Council.
(Ord. 1656, passed 8-31-1983; Ord. 3104, passed 8-7-2017; Ord. 3223, passed 7-
15-2019; Ord. 3365, passed 8-16-2021; Ord. 3523, passed 8-1-2023)
CHAPTER 3: APPOINTED OFFICERS
Section
   
03-03-01   Appointments
   
03-03-03   Terms of office
   
03-03-05   Removal from office
   
03-03-07   Designation of duties
§ 03-03-01 APPOINTMENTS.
   The Mayor shall appoint, with the approval of a majority of the full City
Council: a City Clerk; City Attorney; Public Works Director; Police Chief; Fire
Chief; Director of Finance; City Treasurer; Director of Aviation; Human
Resources Director; Community Development Director; and Parks and Recreation
Director. The Mayor may appoint, with the approval of a majority of the full
City Council, such other officers as are deemed necessary for the efficient
operation of the business of the municipality. If the Mayor’s nomination for an
appointed office is rejected, the city shall follow the process in Idaho Code §
50-205.
(Ord. 2871, passed 3-7-2011; Ord. 3495, passed 4-4-2023; Ord. 3516, passed 7-5-
2023; Ord. 3617, passed 8-5-2024; Ord. 3640, passed 11-18-2024; Ord. 3701,
passed 8-4-2025)
§ 03-03-03 TERMS OF OFFICE.
   Appointed officers shall hold their position until their resignation or
removal. Removal of an appointed officer may be initiated by the Mayor and
confirmed by majority vote of the full City Council, or by unanimous vote of
the full City Council as provided in Idaho Code § 50-206.
(Ord. 1711, passed 10-14-1985; Ord. 3516, passed 7-5-2023; Ord. 3701, passed 8-
4-2025)
§ 03-03-05 REMOVAL FROM OFFICE.
   The Mayor shall remove from office, by and with the consent and advice of
four members of the City Council, any appointed officer of the city, any member
of the board or commission whose removal from office is not otherwise provided
for.
(Ord. 1118, passed 12-4-1967)
§ 03-03-07 DESIGNATION OF DUTIES.
   Whenever there is a question or dispute as to the respective duties or
powers of any appointed officer of the city, the question or dispute shall be
settled by the Mayor, and the Mayor shall have the power to delegate to any
appointed officer any duty which is to be performed when no specific officer
has been directed to perform that duty.
CHAPTER 5: MAYOR
Section
   
03-05-01   Election
   
03-05-03   Conflicting interests
   
03-05-05   Work hours; office space
   
03-05-07   Vacancies in office
   
03-05-09   Powers and duties
   
03-05-11   Decisions of Council
§ 03-05-01 ELECTION.
   The Mayor shall be elected for a four-year term and shall serve until his or
her successor is elected and qualified as provided by statute. A majority of
the votes for any candidate running for the office of Mayor shall be required
for election to that office. In the event no candidate receives a majority of
the votes cast, there shall be a runoff election between the two candidates
receiving the highest number of votes cast. Said runoff election shall be
conducted in cooperation with the County Clerk as provided by statute.
(Ord. 1048, passed 8-2-1965; Ord. 3322, passed 4-5-2021)
§ 03-05-03 CONFLICTING INTERESTS.
   The Mayor shall not engage in any economic endeavor that conflicts with the
duties of the office. Upon being sworn in as Mayor, the Mayor shall resign any
employment, appointed position or elected position, including a City Council
position, with the city.
(Ord. 2701, passed 9-17-2007)
§ 03-05-05 WORK HOURS; OFFICE SPACE.
   (A)   Work hours. The Mayor shall devote not less than 40 hours per week to
performing the duties of the office, excepting therefrom holiday and vacation
periods as established by the Mayor and Council.
   (B)   Office space. The Mayor and Council shall provide offices in the City
Hall for the Mayor.
(Ord. 1825, passed 10-2-1989)
§ 03-05-07 VACANCIES IN OFFICE.
   In case of a temporary vacancy in the office of Mayor due to absence or
disability, the President of the Council shall exercise the office of Mayor
during such disability or temporary absence and until the Mayor shall return.
When a vacancy occurs in the office of Mayor by reason of death, resignation or
permanent disability, the City Council shall fill the vacancy from within or
without the Council as may be deemed in the best interests of the city, and
appointee shall serve until the next general city election, at which election a
Mayor shall be elected for the full four-year term.
§ 03-05-09 POWERS AND DUTIES.
   (A)   Power and authority. The Mayor shall be the Chief Executive Officer of
the city, shall preside over the meetings of the Council and shall perform such
duties as may be required of him or her by law. He or she shall have
supervision over all of the executive officers and employees of the city and
shall have the power and authority to inspect all books and records pertaining
to city affairs and kept by any officer or employee of the city.
   (B)   Membership on Committees and Commissions. The Mayor shall be an ex
officio member of all committees and commissions existing under the city code.
   (C)   Messages to Council. The Mayor shall deliver to the Council such
information and such recommendations as, in his or her opinion, will be of
benefit to the city.
   (D)   Special meetings. The Mayor shall have the power to call special
meetings of the City Council, the object of which shall be submitted to the
Council in writing; the call and object, as well as the disposition thereof,
shall be entered upon the journal by the Clerk. One-half plus one of the
members of the full Council shall also have the power to call special meetings
of the City Council, the object of which shall be submitted to the Council in
writing; the call and object, as well as the disposition thereof, shall be
entered upon the journal of the Clerk.
   (E)   Mayor to sign contacts. The Mayor is authorized and empowered to sign
his or her name, official for and in behalf of, the municipality on all
contracts, documents and papers to which the municipality is a party, and to
require that the conditions of any instrument are faithfully performed. The
Mayor is authorized and empowered to enter into standard form lease agreements
with tenants at the City Industrial Airport, said standard form lease agreement
being adopted, from time to time, by resolution of the City Council. The Mayor
may borrow money on the credit of the municipality when so authorized by the
Council.
   (F)   Jurisdiction. The Mayor shall have the jurisdiction over all places
within five miles of the corporate limits of the municipality for the
enforcement of any health or quarantine ordinances and regulations and shall
have jurisdiction in all matters, excepting taxation, within one mile of the
corporate limits of the municipality.
   (G)   Requiring aid. The Mayor is hereby authorized to call on every male
inhabitant of the municipality of the age of 21 or over to aid him or her in
enforcing the law.
   (H)   Additional duties. The Mayor shall perform all of the duties required
of Mayors under the provisions of Idaho Code Title 50, Chapter 3, and such
other duties as may be reasonably required by the City Council.
   (I)   Drought conditions. The Mayor is hereby authorized to declare the
existence of drought-like conditions and, with the advice of the Public Works
Director, to defer landscaping requirements for development until a date
certain, said date to extend no further than six months from the date of such
declaration without the consent of the City Council, with such conditions as
the Mayor may deem appropriate.
(Ord. 1118, passed 12-4-1967; Ord. 1188, passed 3-16-1970; Ord. 3321, passed 1-
19-2021; Ord. 3361, passed 8-2-2021)
§ 03-05-11 DECISIONS OF COUNCIL.
   (A)   Vote. The Mayor shall have the vote on any decision to be made by the
Council only when the Council is equally divided.
   (B)   Veto. The Mayor shall have the power to veto or sign any law passed by
the Council; provided, that any law vetoes by the Mayor may be passed over his
or her veto by a vote of two-thirds of the elected members of the Council, and
should the Mayor neglect or refuse to sign any law and return the same with his
or her objections, in writing, at the next regular meeting of the Council, the
same shall become a law without his or her signature.
CHAPTER 7: CITY CLERK
Section
   
03-07-01   Appointment and supervision
   
03-07-03   Qualifications and job requirements
   
03-07-05   Powers and duties
§ 03-07-01 APPOINTMENT AND SUPERVISION.
   There is hereby created the position of City Clerk, a position which shall
be filled by appointment as provided in §
03-03-01. The City Clerk shall work under the general guidance and direction of
the Mayor.
(Ord. 1763, passed 12-7-1987)
§ 03-07-03 QUALIFICATIONS AND JOB REQUIREMENTS.
   (A)   Required skills and knowledge. The City Clerk shall be or have:
      (1)   Skilled in data entry, typing and general office procedures and
filing systems;
      (2)   Good knowledge of the organization and functions of city
government;
      (3)   Ability to acquire knowledge of state and local statutes pertaining
to Council proceedings; and
      (4)   Ability to write clear and accurate reports on complex subjects.
   (B)   Acceptable education and experience.
      (1)   High school graduate or equivalent;
      (2)   College level courses in business and public administration
preferred; and
      (3)   Considerable experience in city government desirable or an
equivalent combination of education and experience.
   (C)   Necessary special requirements. The City Clerk must be bondable and
must maintain a valid state driver’s license.
(Ord. 1763, passed 12-7-1987)
§ 03-07-05 POWERS AND DUTIES.
   (A)   General statement of duties. The City Clerk is responsible for all of
the official documents of the municipality and shall act as Clerk of the
governing body. The Clerk performs other duties as assigned or required by the
position.
   (B)   Supervision exercised. The City Clerk supervises a small staff of the
City Clerk’s office.
   (C)   Illustrative examples of duties. The City Clerk:
      (1)   Directs the custody of all ordinances, resolutions, contracts and
all other official documents of the city;
      (2)   Directs the updating of the city code;
      (3)   Attests the Mayor’s signature on official documents of the city;
      (4)   Administers official oaths for the city;
      (5)   Maintains a legislative history record of all items which have
appeared before the Council;
      (6)   Supervises the microfilming and maintenance of all permanent
records of the city;
      (7)   Directs the conduct of all municipal elections;
      (8)   Attends all City Council meetings and acts as Clerk of the Council
at these meetings;
      (9)   Directs the preparation of the official minutes of Council
meetings;
      (10)   Is responsible for all details of Council meetings; prepares and
keeps up to date all records and documents of Council business; prepares
Council agenda; notifies persons when they are in appearance at meetings and
sees that the required documents are assembled and available;
      (11)   Notifies interested parties of Council action;
      (12)   Publishes reports, ordinances and legal notices; maintains custody
of official Council minutes and answers inquiries regarding Council activities;
prepares periodic and special reports of Council activities; and
      (13)   Prepares estimated budget requirements; prepares specialized
technical and financial reports.
(Ord. 1763, passed 12-7-1987)

Section

§ 03-11-01 APPOINTMENT AND SUPERVISION.
   There is hereby created the position of Human Resources Director, a position
which shall be filled by appointment as provided in §
03-03-01. The Human Resources Director shall work under the general guidance
and direction of the Mayor.
(Ord. 2871, passed 3-7-2011)
§ 03-11-03 QUALIFICATIONS AND JOB REQUIREMENTS.
   (A)   Required skills and knowledge.
      (1)   Good oral and written communication skills and comprehensive
knowledge of office administration principles and practices;
      (2)   Comprehensive knowledge of the general principles of local, state
and federal government organization and operation; and
      (3)   Ability to plan, direct, organize, manage and implement the city’s
compensation and benefits package and personnel policies; ensure compliance
with all federal and state employment practice laws; prepare and deliver oral
presentations; maintain records and prepare reports; prioritize and schedule
work; interpret, apply and explain laws, policies and procedures; and work
independently with little direction.
   (B)   Acceptable education and experience.
      (1)   Graduation from an accredited college or university with a
bachelor’s or higher degree in public administration, business administration
or other related field;
      (2)   Considerable experience in public management and administration;
and
      (3)   Any equivalent combination of experience, education and training
which provides the knowledge, skills and abilities necessary to perform the
work.
(Ord. 2871, passed 3-7-2011)
§ 03-11-05 POWERS AND DUTIES.
   (A)   General statement of duties. The Human Resources Director plans,
directs, organizes, manages and implements the city’s compensation and benefits
package and personnel policies; coordinates with the city officials, department
managers and employees; prepares and develops annual budgets and monitors
expenditures; develops, presents and implements training and educational
materials and programs for city employees; reviews employment laws and policies
to ensure compliance; and develops and administers the city’s compensation and
pay plans.
   (B)   Supervision exercised. The Human Resources Director exercises
oversight for all personnel related activities. He or she works closely with
the Mayor, officials and department heads to coordinate, implement and ensure
policy compliance. Direct supervision is exercised over the human resources
staff.
(Ord. 2871, passed 3-7-2011)

CHAPTER 13: CITY ATTORNEY
Section
   
03-13-01   Appointment
   
03-13-03   Powers and duties
§ 03-13-01 APPOINTMENT.
   The City Attorney shall be appointed as provided in §
03-03-01. He or she shall hold office for the duration of his or her
appointment unless sooner removed by the Mayor with the concurrence of the
Council.
§ 03-13-03 POWERS AND DUTIES.
   (A)   Advice. The Attorney shall be the legal advisor of the municipality
and shall render advice on all legal questions affecting the municipality
whenever requested to do so by any municipal official. Upon request by the
Mayor or by the City Council, he or she shall reduce any such opinion to
writing.
   (B)   Suits and actions. The City Attorney shall prosecute and defend any
and all suits or actions at law or equity to which the municipality may be a
party, or in which it may be interested, or which may be brought against or by
any officer of the municipality on behalf of the municipality, or in the
capacity of such person as an officer of the municipality.
   (C)   Enforce judgments. It shall be the duty of the City Attorney to see to
the full enforcement of all judgments or decrees rendered or entered in favor
of the municipality, and of all similar interlocutory orders.
   (D)   Special assessments. It shall be the duty of the City Attorney to see
to the completion of all special assessment proceedings and condemnation
proceedings.
   (E)   Ordinances and documents. It shall be the duty of the City Attorney to
draft or supervise the phraseology of any contract, lease or other document or
instrument, to which the municipality may be a party and, upon the request of
the City Council, to draft ordinances covering any subjects within the power of
the municipality.
CHAPTER 15: CITY TREASURER
Section
   
03-15-01   General statement of duties
   
03-15-03   Supervision received
   
03-15-05   Supervision exercised

§ 03-15-01 GENERAL STATEMENT OF DUTIES.
   Performs a variety of administrative, supervisory and professional tasks
related to the directing, controlling and monitoring of the day-to-day cash
management activities of the city; provides highly responsible and complex
administrative and policy support to the organization; assists city departments
in cash management and related financing activities; makes recommendations
regarding the implementation of cash procedures and policies; and performs
related work as required.
(Ord. 3447, passed 8-18-2022)
§ 03-15-03 SUPERVISION RECEIVED.
   Appointed by the Mayor with consent of the City Council. Works under the
direct supervision of the Mayor and the Council’s Finance Committee.
(Ord. 3447, passed 8-18-2022)
§ 03-15-05 SUPERVISION EXERCISED.
   Hires, trains, supervises and evaluates all Finance Department staff.
(Ord. 3447, passed 8-18-2022)
§ 03-15-07 ESSENTIAL DUTIES.
   The Treasurer shall be the custodian of all monies belonging to the city;
shall account for each fund or appropriation made in its annual budget
appropriation or otherwise directed by the City Council. Such accounting shall
track the debits and credits relating thereto; shall render a monthly
accounting to the City Council; shall also make available credit and debit
details of all such accounts when required by the Mayor or by action of the
governing board; shall make quarterly Treasurer’s reports for public view;
shall keep a record of all outstanding bonds against the city showing the
number, amount of each and to whom said bonds were issued and when any bonds
are purchased, paid or canceled; shall make an annual report; and shall, upon
notification by the State Controller, comply with the accounting and fiscal
reporting requirements set forth in the uniform accounting manual for local
governmental entities authorized under Idaho Code § 67-1075. The Treasurer
shall also have any additional duties described in Idaho Code § 50-208.
(Ord. 3447, passed 8-18-2022)
§ 03-15-09 OTHER ESSENTIAL DUTIES (ILLUSTRATIVE ONLY).
   (A)   Directs, manages and evaluates the financial service operations,
programs and activities of the city;
   (B)   Develops investment strategies in consultation with the Finance
Director;
   (C)   Prepares the monthly Council cash report;
   (D)   Trains city personnel in cash management policies and procedures;
   (E)   Prepares the city’s annual financial report and reviews the auditing
procedure to ensure compliance with state and federal regulations;
   (F)   Coordinates the activities of the audit staff members in cooperation
with other departments to ensure a proper, efficient and responsible use of the
financial management information system;
   (G)   Directs the strategic planning, policy development, data collections
and reporting activities of the Finance Department;
   (H)   Oversees all general city accounting, including monitoring accounts
payables, utility billing and payroll and other financial resources;
   (I)   Analyzes the city’s daily cash flow to determine the necessary
operating cash balances and invests all excess funds to ensure safety,
liquidity and yield;
   (J)   Works closely with department directors and managers to provide cash
management policy guidance and to follow-up on director’s assignments;
   (K)   Notifies the Finance Director, Mayor and department directors on
financial issues;
   (L)   Oversees, reconciles and accounts for all city revenue and monitors
utility account receipts;
   (M)   Accounting software: coordinates computer support for financial and
bank software and modules; provides staff training; resolves operation related
issues and staff questions; and assists in establishing security access for
administrative staff;
   (N)   City Urban Renewal Agency: assists Finance Director in audit and
budget preparation;
   (O)   Library: provides cash management support to the Library Director,
including recommending and managing investments and maintaining investment
policies;
   (P)   Grants: files federal and state grant reports and prepares SEFA and
audit schedules;
   (Q)   Debt: responsible for bond covenant compliance and annual reporting;
   (R)   Budget: prepares initial extended Budgeting Department reports; trains
city staff in budget report preparation and submission; and uploads and
reconciles adopted budget files into extended budgeting and general ledger;
   (S)   Assists in annual budget preparations; edits, updates and creates
budget reports; uploads the annual budget tracking software; monitors budget
revenues and disbursements; and prepares monthly Council Revenue and Cash
Report;
   (T)   Monitors budgetary activities and investigates exceptions;
   (U)   Prepares the annual budget amendment, including gathering all dates,
analyzing results and presenting a final report to the Finance Director, Mayor,
City Council and the public;
   (V)   Provides recommendations to the Finance Director, City Council,
department directors and city employees on proper internal controls, budgeting
practices, financing methods and other cash management functions;
   (W)   Responsible for distribution of annual budget;
   (X)   Audit: prepares year-end statements, audit schedules, worksheets, cash
and investment audit work papers, and footnotes associated with the city’s
Annual Finance Report, and provides technical information to auditors;
completes year-end closing entries; assists with audit fieldwork; interfaces
with external auditors to respond to questions or requests for information;
maintains the reporting system within the city’s engagement system and
supporting schedules; and distributes annual audits to Federal Clearing House
agencies;
   (Y)   Records closing journal entries to general ledger;
   (Z)   Maintains current knowledge of organizational policies and procedures
relating to federal and state policies, directives and current accounting
standards;
   (AA)   Prepares or directs the preparation of financial statements, audit
work papers, financial position forecasts, budget status reports and other
requested reports;
   (BB)   Staff support: cross-trains in accounting tasks and all application
modules in Springbrook Financial Software;
   (CC)   Hires, trains, supervises and evaluates all Finance Department staff;
   (DD)   Keeps immediate supervisor and designated others fully and accurately
informed concerning work progress, including present and potential work
problems and suggestions for new or improved ways of addressing such problems;
   (EE)   Attends approved meetings, conferences, workshops, training sessions
and reviews publications and audio-visual materials to become and remain
current on the principles, practices and new developments in assigned work
areas;
   (FF)   Responds to citizens’ questions and comments in a courteous and
timely manner;
   (GG)   Trains, assigns, prioritizes, supervises, motivates and evaluates the
work of assigned employees;
   (HH)   Communicates and respects the opinions of others and maintains a
positive and professional working relationship with city officials, employees,
supervisors and others; and
   (II)   Perform all other duties as may be assigned by the Mayor or Mayor and
Council.
(Ord. 3447, passed 8-18-2022)
§ 03-15-11 REQUIRED KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES.
   (A)   Demonstrated knowledge of the principles and practices of public
administration, specifically municipal government and finance;
   (B)   Demonstrated knowledge of the general principles of local, state and
federal government organization and operation;
   (C)   Demonstrated knowledge of banking practices;
   (D)   Demonstrated knowledge of and ability to apply effective management
techniques and budgetary procedures;
   (E)   Demonstrated knowledge of the duties, responsibilities and authorities
of each department within the city;
   (F)   Demonstrated knowledge of the practices, methods and laws related to
municipal bond financing;
   (G)   Thorough knowledge of methods and procedures involved in the receipt
and disbursement of large sums of money;
   (H)   Working knowledge of the principles of supervision;
   (I)   Ability to evaluate complex financial systems and efficiently
formulate and install accounting methods, procedures, forms and records as it
relates to budgeting;
   (J)   Ability to prepare and explain financial reports;
   (K)   Ability to prepare long-range fiscal forecasts and budgeting;
   (L)   Ability to perform financial analysis;
   (M)   Ability to plan, lay out, supervise and coordinate the work of a small
staff of employees;
   (N)   Ability to communicate clearly and effectively, both verbally and in
writing;
   (O)   Ability to utilize active listening techniques;
   (P)   Ability to utilize long-range planning skills for the development of
department plans;
   (Q)   Ability to deal tactfully with citizens, subordinates, department
staff and local, state and federal representatives;
   (R)   Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with
elected officials, city supervisor and employees, business leaders, other
government agencies and general public;
   (S)   Ability to train, assign, motivate, supervise and evaluate the work of
others;
   (T)   Ability to operate a personal computer using program applications
appropriate to assigned duties and responsibilities;
   (U)   Ability to quickly learn and put to use new skills and knowledge
brought about by rapidly changing information and/or technology; and
   (V)   Integrity, ingenuity and inventiveness in the performance of assigned
tasks.
(Ord. 3447, passed 8-18-2022)
§ 03-15-13 ACCEPTABLE EXPERIENCE AND TRAINING.
   (A)   Graduation from an accredited college or university with a bachelor’s
or master’s degree in public administration, finance or other related field;
   (B)   Five years of progressively responsible finance and accounting
experience in public and financial management and administration; and/or
   (C)   Any equivalent combination of experience, education and training which
provides the knowledge, skills and abilities necessary to perform the work.
(Ord. 3447, passed 8-18-2022)
CHAPTER 16: CITY FINANCE DIRECTOR

§ 03-16-05 ESSENTIAL DUTIES.

planning activities;
   (H)   Develops and directs the implementation of finance related goals,
objectives, policies, procedures and work practices;
   (I)   Prepares and recommends long-range financial plans for city services
and programs; and develops specific proposals for action on current and future
city needs;
   (J)   Oversees the city’s budget by managing the development and
implementation of goals and priorities; and meets with departments to review
work plans and budgeting needs;
   (K)   Establishes appropriate service and staffing levels; and assesses and
monitors staff workload and support systems;
   (L)   Reviews and analyzes financial methods, activities and performance to
find ways to increase effectiveness and improve results and/or the effect on
economies;
   (M)   Makes clear and concise presentations to the City Council;
   (N)   Presents the Mayor’s recommended budgets to the City Council and
general public;
   (O)   Responsible for city municipal financing and bonding; and works with
bonding agencies to initiate and apply for needed financing;
   (P)   Provides recommendations to the City Council, department directors,
accountants and city employees on proper internal controls, budgeting
practices, financing methods and other accounting functions;
   (Q)   Directs the centralized accounting and reporting function for the
city;
   (R)   Maintains current knowledge of organizational policies and procedures,
federal and state policies and directives and current accounting standards;
   (S)   Directs pre-audit and internal audit functions;
   (T)   Serves as a liaison to external independent audits;
   (U)   Responds to information requests from departments on accounting
systems and reporting requirements;
   (V)   Prepares and directs the preparation of the annual budget, business
activity reports, financial position forecasts and other required reports;
   (W)   Monitors, interprets and evaluates changes in laws and regulations
related to financial activities and functions;
   (X)   Develops and prepares ordinances, regulations, policies and procedures
and revisions related to financial activities;
   (Y)   Keeps immediate supervisor and designated others fully and accurately
informed concerning work progress, including present and potential work

   (Z)   Attends approved meetings, conferences, workshops, training sessions
and reviews publications and audio-visual materials to become and remain
current on the principles, practices and new developments in assigned work

   (AA)   Responds to citizens’ questions and comments in a courteous and

   (BB)   Communicates and coordinates regularly with others to maximize the

   (CC)   Advises the Mayor and department directors on financial issues and

   (DD)   Establishes financial priorities and objectives which often affect
multiple departments;
   (EE)   Creates, organizes, appoints and directs members of inter-
departmental committees for the purpose of addressing citywide financial or
project related needs;
   (FF)   Maintains an effective relationship with the City Council by
recommending financial policies, providing reports and developing methods for
carrying out the Council’s intentions that are in compliance with ordinances
and in the best interest of the citizens of the city;
   (GG)   Informs and advises the City Council on significant administrative
actions, controversial matters and public interactions; and
   (HH)   Develops, recommends and implements financial policies to attain the
long- and short-range goals of the city.
(Ord. 3447, passed 8-18-2022)

§ 03-17-01 APPOINTMENT.
   There is hereby created the position of Chief of Police, a position which
shall be filled as provided in §
03-03-01. The Chief of Police works under the general guidance and direction of
the Mayor.
(Ord. 1766, passed 12-7-1987)
§ 03-17-03 QUALIFICATIONS AND JOB REQUIREMENTS.
   (A)   Required skill, knowledge and abilities.
      (1)   Considerable knowledge of laws, codes, statutes, ordinances,
policies and procedures and standard police operations.
      (2)   Ability to supervise, schedule and coordinate activities of staff.
To represent the Department effectively; to communicate clearly and concisely,
both orally and in writing; to establish and maintain effective working
relationships; and, to make sound decisions.
   (B)   Acceptable education and experience. The Chief of Police shall have a
bachelor’s degree and ten years of municipal law enforcement experience, or an
equivalent combination of education and experience.
   (C)   Necessary special requirements. The Chief of Police shall have and
maintain a valid state driver’s license.
(Ord. 1766, passed 12-7-1987)
§ 03-17-05 POWERS AND DUTIES.
   (A)   Relating to the Police Department.
      (1)   Responsible for the operation, administration and coordination of
the City Police Department;
      (2)   Performs other duties as assigned or required by the position; and
      (3)   Exercises supervision of officers and staff directly or through
subordinate supervisors.
   (B)   Illustrative examples of duties.
      (1)   Coordinates activities in law enforcement and security for the
protection of life and property;
      (2)   Delegates work activities and duties to division commanders as
appropriate;
      (3)   Develops and administers schools and conferences;
      (4)   Directs and reviews planning, research and budget activities;
      (5)   Administers the Department’s personnel system, including
recruitment, promotions, performance evaluations, discipline, counseling and
assignments;
      (6)   Provides for the execution of all departmental and city rules,
regulations, policies and procedures;
      (7)   Confers with citizens concerning complaints, problems, requests,
suggestions and directs action when appropriate;
      (8)   Routinely shares information with Mayor and City Council and
submits monthly report of activity and trends;
      (9)   Performs a wide variety of public relations functions;
      (10)   Attends meetings, serves on committees and boards, representing
the Department and the city; attends conferences and meeting with
representatives of other law enforcement and allied agencies;
      (11)   Develops and maintains liaison with local, state and county law
enforcement agencies and private entities; and
      (12)   On call 24 hours each day.
   (C)   Recovered and stolen property. The Chief of Police and his or her
designated agents shall have the custody of all lost, abandoned or stolen
property recovered within the municipality.
(Ord. 1766, passed 12-7-1987)

rules, regulations, policies and procedures;

      (11)   Shall be on call 24 hours each day.
