§ 04-01-01 WATER DEPARTMENT.
   (A)   Department established. There is hereby established a Water Department
which shall consist of such personnel as may be provided by the Mayor and the
City Council and the operation of which shall be under the direction of the
Water Superintendent.
   (B)   Responsibility. It shall be the responsibility of all members of the
Water Department to operate and maintain all the equipment and facilities used
in the procurement and delivery of domestic water and take every possible
precaution to, at all times, ensure the purity of the water and safety and
health of the public.
(Ord. 1618, passed 10-12-1982)
§ 04-01-03 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this chapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   CITY. The City of Caldwell, Canyon County, Idaho, or its authorized or
designated agent, representative or deputy thereof.
   CITY WATER SERVICE LINE. The portion of a water service line that runs from
its connection with the city water main to and including the corporation stop,
valve box and meter yoke installed in the service line. The water service is
owned and maintained by the city and will usually be installed within the
limits of the public right-of-way or utility easement.
   CITY WATER SYSTEM. Includes all components and facilities of the water
system that is owned, operated and maintained by the city to provide domestic
water supply.
   MASTER WATER PLAN. Any document which the city has accepted or may accept by
official action of the City Council which describes or otherwise indicates an
overall view of proposed future water needs, water main sizing and/or water
main spacing.
   OWNER. Refers to the property owner, tenant, developer, lease holder and the
like that is served by the city water system.
   PRIVATE FIRE SERVICE CONNECTION. A separate and independent connection from
the city water main that connects directly to a sprinkler system or fire
control device that has been, or is to be, installed in any building for the
purpose of fire control within the specific building and said connection is to
be for no other purpose.
   PRIVATE WATER SERVICE LINE. The water service line from the city water meter
to and throughout the property and building being served.
   PRIVATE WATER SYSTEM. Any domestic water system that is not owned, operated
or maintained by the city.
   PROPERTY. Refers to all property, whether privately or publicly owned,
within the service limits of the city water system, excluding therefrom lands
that have been dedicated for public street or highway rights-of-way.
   WATER MAIN. Any pipe owned by the city for the purpose of transportation
and/or distribution of water to serve more than one water service line or user.
(Ord. 1618, passed 10-12-1982; Ord. 2831, passed 5-17-2010)
§ 04-01-05 APPLICABILITY.
   The provisions of this chapter shall apply to all property within the
corporate limits of the city and any special users outside of the corporate
limits of the city, including all property owned or occupied by the United
States of America, the state and the county.
(Ord. 1618, passed 10-12-1982)
§ 04-01-07 POWERS AND AUTHORITY OF CITY AUTHORIZED REPRESENTATIVE.
   The city, through its authorized representative bearing proper credentials
and identification, shall be permitted at proper and reasonable hours of the
day to enter all properties, premises or buildings to which water is furnished
from the city water system for testing or for any other purpose necessary for
the proper administration of the water system in accordance with provisions of
this chapter, regardless of the presence or lack thereof of any easements. All
entry and subsequent work, if any, on said properties, premises or buildings
shall be done in a workmanlike manner. Also, the city, through its authorized
representative bearing proper credentials and identification, shall be
permitted to enter all private properties through which the city holds an
easement for the purpose of, but not limited to, inspection, observation,
repair and maintenance of any portion of the city water system lying within
said easements. All entry and subsequent work, if any, on said easement shall
be done in a workmanlike manner.
(Ord. 2831, passed 5-17-2010)
§ 04-01-09 WATER CONNECTIONS, CONSTRUCTION REGULATIONS.
   (A)   Separate connections required. Each separate building shall be
connected with the water main through a city water service line, which includes
a meter. Each individual airport hangar unit, even if all airport hangars are
contained within the same building, shall be connected individually with the
water main through a city water service line, which includes a meter. The
city’s portion of the water service line ends at the meter. Individual service
requirements for condominium projects shall be as per §
11-04-05. Subsequent to investigation by the City Engineer, the City Council
may grant permission for a single meter to serve more than one water consumer.
Upon a granting of an exemption, the base water rate shall be adjusted to
reflect the number of water consumers on a single meter.
   (B)   Application for service connection and permit to use water.
Application to have a city water service, including a meter, installed shall be
made by the owner of the premises to the Water Superintendent or other assigned
officer. The application shall contain a full, true and accurate statement of
the size of the connection, a description of the premises upon which such
connection is to be made, together with the full name of such owners to conform
to the rules and regulations provided for the city water system. No water shall
be introduced into any connection heretofore or hereafter made therewith unless
the permit has first been approved by the Water Superintendent or other
designated officer, and all fees set forth in the rate schedule adopted by
resolution of the City Council have been paid.
   (C)   Meters property of the city. All meters shall be and remain the
property of the city, and in the event of a meter getting out of order and
failing to register, the consumer shall be charged in accordance with the rate
schedule adopted by resolution of the City Council.
   (D)   Private water service line. All materials and workmanship used in the
installation of private water service lines shall conform to city
specifications and codes. The furnishing of all labor and materials shall be
the sole responsibility of the owner.
   (E)   Private fire service connection. The installation of a private fire
service connection shall comply in all respects to the requirements for a city
water service line, and the owner or his or her agent will be required to pay
for all costs for connection and extension of the facility from the city water
main.
   (F)   No connections outside the city. Requests for water line connections
outside the city limits are governed by the “service connection policy outside
the city limits,” which policy shall be adopted by resolution of the City
Council except by special permit granted by the City Council.
   (G)   Extension of city water mains and water main fee.
      (1)   All proposed extensions of the city water mains to service
undeveloped areas within the existing corporate limits or newly annexed areas
shall comply with existing policies, specifications, master plans or
requirements established by the City Engineer. The plans for all extensions to
the city water mains shall be prepared under the direction of and signed by a
registered professional engineer as per the licensing requirements of the state
code, and three copies of said plans shall be filed with the city. In approving
a plan for extension to the city water mains, the city reserves the right to
stipulate other requirements such as a special permit fee, rights-of-way
limits, sequence of construction, time limits for having existing service
disrupted, the filing of a financial guarantee and other similar measures as
may be required to protect the public. No work shall commence on any such
extension of the city water mains until the extension project has been approved
by the City Council and a written permit has been issued. A permit shall not be
issued until all applicable fees have been paid.
      (2)   All water main extensions and appurtenances made for the purpose of
serving the development shall be constructed at the expense of the landowner
and/or developer by a qualified contractor in accordance with city
specifications and subject to conditions and fees which may be established by
the city.
      (3)   The city shall charge a water main fee on all new buildings and
developments that will be provided water service. The amount of the fee and the
methods of derivation shall be in accordance with the rate schedule adopted by
resolution of the City Council.
   (H)   Requirements for extending water service outside the city limits. All
extensions of water service outside the city limits shall be recommended by the
City Engineer and approved by the City Council on a case-by-case basis. Said
extensions of service shall be granted only when in the best interest of the
city. The extension of service is a privilege and not a right. In determining
whether to allow an extension of water service, the following criteria shall be
considered.
      (1)   The extension of water service only shall not be permitted except
by approval of the City Council.
      (2)   The City Council may, at its option, require prepayment of water
hookup fees.
      (3)   The extent to which the extension of water service would create an
adverse impact upon existing facilities or create economic burdens for future
operation and maintenance of the city water system.
      (4)   Water main extensions shall be made at no cost to the city. Mains
shall be adequately sized for future growth, and no credit will be allowed for
additional costs associated with oversized mains required by the city either
within the proposed development or in the extension of city lines.
      (5)   The extent to which the city water system has adequate capacity to
serve existing development, the proposed development for which the extension is
requested and all probable development within the extension requested, and all
probable development within the city and between the city and the proposed
development.
      (6)   The owner of the proposed development must consent to annexation by
the city and at the city’s option and convenience. This agreement will be
binding on the development.
   (I)   Construction methods and materials. The materials and methods used for
construction of city water service lines, private water service lines, water
mains or water system appurtenances shall conform to the requirements of all
codes and specifications as may be adopted by the City Council. The city may
reject any materials or workmanship for cause and, upon such order, the
rejected materials shall be removed and replaced with approved material.
   (J)   Illegal connections.
      (1)   It shall be unlawful for any person to make or cause to be made any
connection with the city water main or to introduce or cause to be introduced
water from the city water main into any connection made therewith unless a
permit has been first duly issued for such purpose by the Building Inspector in
compliance and conformity with the provisions of this chapter and the rules and
regulations of the city that are now or may hereafter be established therefor;
or to cause a connection to become in noncompliance with the provisions of this
chapter and the rules and regulations of the city that are now or may hereafter
be established; or to interfere with or injure any hydrant, pipe connection,
meter or any property of the city water system. Violation of this provision
shall be a misdemeanor.
      (2)   The city, by and through the Building Inspector, shall give notice
in writing to the owner and/or occupant of any premises connected to and served
by city water main in all cases in which said connections are illegal. Said
notice shall state the violation and require that the violations be cured
within 30 days from notice thereof or water service will be discontinued.
      (3)   In the event that said illegal connection continues beyond the 30-
day period, the city is authorized to discontinue water service to said
premises without further notice and until said illegal connection is
discontinued.
      (4)   A violation of this provision is a misdemeanor.
   (K)   Fees.
      (1)   Service connection fees. In addition to any inspection fees, main
extension fees and impact fees, the developer shall be required to pay a
service connection fee. The amount of the service connection fee shall be in
accordance with the rate schedule adopted by resolution of the City Council. A
copy of current service connection fees for various meter sizes will be on file
in the Water Superintendent’s office.
      (2)   Special fee for service outside the city. Service connection and
inspection fees for properties outside the city limits shall be in accordance
with the rate schedule adopted by resolution of the City Council.
      (3)   Impact fees and base charges. The city shall have authority to
assess the developer and/or landowner fees in addition to the aforementioned
fees. These additional fees are termed impact and capital improvement base fees
and are for the purpose of providing a more equitable distribution of city
water system costs relating to such items as water supply development, storage,
transmission lines and other off-site improvements and shall be in accordance
with the rate schedule approved by resolution of the City Council.
   (L)   Water and fire hydrant water line dedications. A maintenance and
operation easement shall be granted to the city for any water mains and/or
appurtenances that are intended and/or required to be dedicated to the city
that are located outside of dedicated public right-of-way and shall be granted
prior to issuance of a final certificate of occupancy. Additionally, all water
lines servicing fire hydrants, including the fire hydrants themselves, shall be
dedicated to the public for ownership, operation and maintenance. Requests for
dedication shall be received, reviewed and cleared for City Council agenda
placement prior to issuance of a final certificate of occupancy.
(Ord. 1618, passed 10-12-1982; Ord. 1940, passed 3-16-1992; Ord. 2558, passed
10-17-2005; Ord. 2831, passed 5-17-2010)
§ 04-01-11 RESTRICTIONS ON WATER USE.
   No person supplied with water from the city water mains will be entitled to
use it for any other purpose than stated in his or her permit, nor shall water
be supplied to other households or businesses, or allowed to be taken off the
premises with the intent of bypassing a service connection.
(Ord. 1618, passed 10-12-1982)
§ 04-01-13 UPKEEP OF SERVICE PIPES AND FIXTURES.
   All service pipes and fixtures on private property are the responsibility of
the property owner and shall be kept in good repair and protected from freezing
at the property owner’s expense. The property owner shall be responsible for
all damages resulting from leaks or breaks in service pipes and fixtures. Water
will not be furnished to a water service where there is a leak in the service
piping or in a fixture, and when a leak is discovered, the water service may be
discontinued immediately. If water service has been discontinued and there is a
leak, it shall not be turned on until all leaks have been repaired.
(Ord. 1940, passed 3-16-1992)
§ 04-01-15 WATER USER CHARGES AND FEES.
   (A)   The water user charges and fees shall be established to cover
operation and maintenance costs of the city water system, and to provide a fund
to pay for capital improvement costs, additions, participation in oversized
extensions to the system, or redemption of bonds that have been used to finance
system improvements, all as a part of the city’s responsibility to provide
adequate domestic water service and facilities for the city. For new
connections, the water user charge is to begin when the meter is turned on.
   (B)   Charges for shut-off and turn on of customer accounts shall be in
accordance with the rate schedule adopted by resolution of the City Council.
   (C)   All owners who derive benefit from the city’s water system shall, in
return for said benefit, pay user charges. Only the benefiting property owner,
or his or her duly authorized agent, may initiate water service. The procedures
for initiating service, disconnecting service, billing of accounts and
processing of delinquent accounts shall be in accordance with policies adopted
by resolution of the City Council.
   (D)   At the initiation or reconnection of service, the city may elect to
collect a security deposit to ensure the ultimate payment of charges and fees.
The procedures for collecting, the amount, the procedures for applying to
delinquent charges and fees and the final disposition of unapplied amounts of
said security deposit shall be in accordance with policies adopted by
resolution of the City Council.
   (E)   The water user charge shall be based on the amount of water used.
Fees, which may include penalties, may be for amounts independent of the amount
of water used. Water user charges and fees shall be in accordance with rates
and amounts established by resolution of the City Council.
(Ord. 1940, passed 3-16-1992; Ord. 2465, passed 7-21-2003)
§ 04-01-17 BILLING ACCOUNTING.
   (A)   Billing frequency. Billing cycle frequency and due dates for accounts
shall be established in the billing policy, as adopted by resolution of the
City Council.
   (B)   Water payments. Payments due the city shall be received and processed
by the Finance Director of the city, in accordance with the state code.
   (C)   Delinquent accounts. Water charges billed shall become delinquent on
the due date. Delinquent accounts shall be processed in accordance with the
billing policy adopted by resolution of the City Council.
(Ord. 1940, passed 3-16-1992)
§ 04-01-19 UTILITY BOARD ESTABLISHED.
   There is hereby a Board established and appointed by the Mayor of the city
to hear requests for variances to established policies adopted by resolution of
the City Council, and to request billing adjustments. The Board shall inform
the customer of the right to appeal adverse decisions pursuant to city
ordinance. (See
Title 1, Chapter 5.)
(Ord. 1940, passed 3-16-1992)
§ 04-01-21 RIGHT OF CITY TO TURN OFF THE WATER SUPPLY.
   The city reserves the right at any time without notice to shut off the water
supply for repairs, extensions or any other reason, and the city shall not be
responsible for damage such as bursting of boilers supplied by direct pressure,
the breaking of any pipes or fixtures or any other damage resulting from the
shutting off of the water.
(Ord. 1618, passed 10-12-1982)
§ 04-01-23 FAILURE OF WATER SUPPLY.
   The city shall not be liable under any circumstance for a deficiency or a
failure in the supply of water whether by the shutting off of the water to make
repairs or connections or for any cause whatsoever.
(Ord. 1618, passed 10-12-1982)
§ 04-01-25 PROHIBITED ACTS.
   (A)   Unlawful use of fire hydrants. It shall be unlawful for any person,
except one duly authorized by the city, to open, close, operate, turn on, turn
off, interfere with, attach any pipe or hose to or connect anything with any
fire hydrant or auxiliary valve belonging to the city. Further, it shall be
unlawful for any person to obstruct the access to any fire hydrant by placing
around or thereon any stone, brick, lumber, dirt or other material, or to
willfully or carelessly injure the hydrant.
   (B)   Malicious or willful waste of water. It shall be unlawful for any
water user to waste water or allow it to be wasted by imperfect water stops,
valves or leaky pipes that are not under the jurisdiction of the city, or to
permit the malicious or willful consumption of water, having no beneficial use.
The city, based on meter readings, will make a determination of where water has
been wasted and shall notify the user of that determination. It shall then be
the user’s responsibility to make the necessary repairs, or to institute
actions that will correct that situation within 60 days of the city’s
notification to the user. All costs incurred including the cost of wasted water
and any repairs shall be the responsibility of the user.
(Ord. 1618, passed 10-12-1982)
§ 04-01-27 TERMINATION FOR NONCOMPLIANCE.
   Service shall be terminated and restored in accordance with the billing
policy and rate schedule adopted by resolution of the City Council.
(Ord. 1940, passed 3-16-1992)
§ 04-01-29 SAVING CLAUSE.
   If any section, division, sentence or provision hereof or the application
thereof to any particular circumstance shall ever be invalid or unenforceable,
such holding shall not affect the remainder hereof, which shall continue in
full force and effect and be applicable to all circumstances to which it may
validly apply.
(Ord. 1618, passed 10-12-1982)
§ 04-01-31 PENALTIES.
   (A)   Any person found to be violating any provision of this chapter shall
be served by the city with a written notice stating the nature of the violation
and provided a specified maximum period of time, said period not to exceed 60
days, for the satisfactory correction thereof. The offender shall, within the
period of time stated in such notice, permanently cease all violations.
   (B)   Any person who shall continue any violation beyond the time limit
provided for in division (A) above shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and, on
conviction thereof, shall be subject to fine and/or imprisonment, up to, but
not exceeding, the maximum penalties set forth in Idaho Code § 50-302, as
amended. Each day in which any such violation shall continue shall be deemed a
separate offense.
   (C)   Any person violating any of the provisions of this chapter shall
become liable to the city for any expense, loss or damage occasioned the city
by reason of such violation.
(Ord. 1618, passed 10-12-1982; Ord. 2669, passed 2-20-2007)
CHAPTER 3: CROSS-CONNECTION CONTROL
Section
   
04-03-01   Definitions
   
04-03-03   New and existing service, testing and inspections
   
04-03-05   Use of backflow prevention device
   
04-03-07   Degree of hazard
   
04-03-09   Additional remedies
   
04-03-11   Violations and penalties
   
04-03-13   Severability
§ 04-03-01 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this chapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   AGENT. An employee of the City Water Department representing the interest of
the city.
   APPROVED DEVICE. A backflow prevention device, of proper design, certified
by the State Division of Environment Quality.
   BACKFLOW. The process of reverse flow of any substance into the city water
system caused by back pressure or backsiphonage.
   CITY WATER SYSTEM. The source, pumping facilities, storage and transmission
and distribution system of the city for providing water for human consumption.
   CROSS-CONNECTION. Any physical connection or arrangement between two
otherwise separate piping systems, one of which contains potable water and the
other any substance whereby the potential for reverse flow exists.
   SUPERINTENDENT. The Superintendent of the Water Department or his or her
authorized representative.
(Ord. 1801, passed 2-6-1989)
§ 04-03-03 NEW AND EXISTING SERVICE, TESTING AND INSPECTIONS.
   (A)   City water service will not be provided to any new user of city water
until a physical inspection by the Superintendent shows no potential cross-
connections exist. Additionally, water service shall be discontinued to any
user with a potential cross-connection on his, her or their premises, until
such time as the proper prevention device is installed and tested.
   (B)   Water service shall not be provided to any new structure built until
it has been inspected for cross-connections and approved by the Superintendent.
   (C)   Periodic inspections shall be made by the agent on all buildings where
the possibility of cross-connections may occur.
(Ord. 1801, passed 2-6-1989)
§ 04-03-05 USE OF BACKFLOW PREVENTION DEVICE.
   When deemed necessary by the Superintendent, an approved device shall be
purchased and installed at the user’s expense on the owner’s property. An
annual operational test shall be conducted by the agent, or other certified
backflow device tester, to ensure the effectiveness of the device. A backflow
device shall be installed whenever materials stored or processed by the user
would present a hazard to health or impair the quality of water provided by the
city water system. Activities requiring a backflow device include, but are not
limited to, the following:
   (A)   Premises having an auxiliary water supply;
   (B)   Premises with intricate plumbing systems which make it difficult to
determine if a cross-connection exists;
   (C)   Premises with entry restrictions making inspection for cross-
connections impractical;
   (D)   Premises with known cross-connections or a history of cross-
connections;
   (E)   Any location where process or cooling substances are pressurized;
   (F)   Premises where hazardous or toxic material are handled and the
possibility of backsiphonage exists; and
   (G)   Backflow prevention devices shall be installed on the following
facilities for the protection of the city water system:
      (1)   Hospitals, clinics and mortuaries;
      (2)   Laboratories;
      (3)   Metal plating industries;
      (4)   Sewage treatment facilities;
      (5)   Food or beverage processing plants;
      (6)   Chemical/industrial plants using a water process;
      (7)   Petroleum storage facilities;
      (8)   Chemical storage or distribution facilities;
      (9)   Tank truck fill stations;
      (10)   Car washes; and
      (11)   Any site specified by the Superintendent or the state as
endangering the quality of the city water system.
(Ord. 1801, passed 2-6-1989)
§ 04-03-07 DEGREE OF HAZARD.
   Minimum backflow protection required shall conform to the following
requirements:
   (A)   An air gap separation or reduced pressure principle device is required
for hazardous or toxic applications;
   (B)   A double check valve assembly shall be installed when an objectionable
but not hazardous substance could come into contact with the city water system;
   (C)   For lawn sprinkler applications, an atmospheric vacuum breaker can be
installed, provided no shut-off valves are installed downstream from the
device; or
   (D)   A pressure vacuum breaker shall be installed when shut-off valves are
located downstream.
(Ord. 1801, passed 2-6-1989)
§ 04-03-09 ADDITIONAL REMEDIES.
   In the event a cross-connection is discovered and not corrected within 90
days, or when inspection access is refused, water service shall be terminated
until such time as the deficiency is corrected. In addition, the agent may have
the appropriate protective device installed, at the owner’s expense, and resume
water service only when all costs have been recouped.
(Ord. 1801, passed 2-6-1989)
§ 04-03-11 VIOLATIONS AND PENALTIES.
   Any person who is found to be guilty of violating any portion of this
chapter shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
(Ord. 1801, passed 2-6-1989)
§ 04-03-13 SEVERABILITY.
   If any one or more sections or divisions this chapter are for any reason
held to be invalid or unconstitutional, such decision shall not affect the
validity of the remaining portions of this chapter, and the same shall remain
in full force and effect.
(Ord. 1801, passed 2-6-1989)
CHAPTER 5: SANITARY SEWER SYSTEM
Section
   
04-05-01   Short title
   
04-05-02   Department created
   
04-05-03   Powers and responsibilities of Department
   
04-05-04   Additional powers
   
04-05-05   Definitions
   
04-05-06   Applicability of chapter
   
04-05-07   Connection to city owned treatment works/POTW; construction
standards
   
04-05-08   Major contributing industry
   
04-05-09   Fees, charges and billing accounts
   
04-05-10   Prohibited acts
   
04-05-11   Severability
   
04-05-12   Effective date
§ 04-05-01 SHORT TITLE.
   This chapter shall be known as the Sewer Treatment Department, Standards and
Service Ordinance.
(Ord. 2064, passed 1-17-1995)
§ 04-05-02 DEPARTMENT CREATED.
   There is hereby created the “City Owned Treatment Works/POTW Department”
which Department shall be under the supervision of the City Engineer/Public
Works Director with the operation of the City Owned Treatment Works/POTW under
the direction of the Treatment Plant Superintendent, which Superintendent shall
be, upon recommendation of the City Engineer/Public Works Director, appointed
by the Mayor and City Council, either as an employee or by an independent
contract.
(Ord. 2064, passed 1-17-1995)
§ 04-05-03 POWERS AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF DEPARTMENT.
   The city owned treatment works/POTW Department shall have the following
powers, duties and responsibilities:
   (A)   To recommend and carry out the city’s responsibility providing for the
repair, rebuilding, connection to and acceptance of its city owned treatment
works/POTW, which includes all aspects of a sewerage system, as defined by
Idaho Code § 50-1029, including the acquiring, constructing, reconstructing,
improving, bettering or extending said works, its management of such works in
the most efficient manner, consisting of sound economy and public advantage to
the end that the service or that the system and the service for which it
provides shall be at the lowest possible cost in conformance with state and
federal law and requirements, all in the promotion of the welfare and
improvement of the health, safety, comfort and convenience of the inhabitants
of the city;
   (B)   To exercise the authority of the city to operate and maintain such
works within and without the boundaries of the city or partially within or
without the boundaries of the city or within any part of the city as especially
authorized; and
   (C)   To prescribe and collect rates, fees, tolls or charges, including levy
of assessment for such rates, fees, tolls or charges against all users,
including governmental units, departments or agencies, including the state and
its subdivisions for the services and facilities furnished by such works or by
the rehabilitation thereof and to provide methods for collection and penalties,
including the denial of service for nonpayment of such rates, fees, tolls or
charges, to the end that the same may be and always remain self-supporting.
(Ord. 2064, passed 1-17-1995)
§ 04-05-04 ADDITIONAL POWERS.
   (A)   Powers and authority of city authorized representative. The
Department, through its authorized representatives, shall be permitted at
proper and reasonable hours of the day to enter all properties, premises or
buildings which are connected to the POTW for testing or for any other purpose
necessary for the proper administration of the sanitary sewer system/POTW in
accordance with the provisions of this chapter, regardless of the presence or
lack thereof of any easements. All entry and subsequent work, if any, on said
properties, premises or buildings shall be done in a workmanlike manner. Also,
the city, through its authorized representative bearing proper credentials and
identification, shall be permitted to enter all private properties through
which the city holds an easement for the purpose of, but not limited to,
inspection, observation, repair, maintenance and replacement of any
appurtenances of the city sanitary sewer system lying within said easements.
All entry and subsequent work, if any, on said easement shall be done in a
workmanlike manner.
   (B)   Rules and regulations. The City Engineer/Public Works Director may
make or prescribe such rules and regulations deemed advisable to implement this
chapter. Such rules are to be in force after approval of the Mayor and City
Council by resolution. Said rules and regulations may cover all aspects of
construction standards, sewer service charge adjustments, charges for sewer
connection, classification of service, exemption from payment for sewer
service, payment for service where building is not connected to the city owned
waterworks.
(Ord. 2064, passed 1-17-1995; Ord. 2831, passed 5-17-2010)
§ 04-05-05 DEFINITIONS.
   (A)   Generally. For the purpose of this chapter, the following definitions
shall apply unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different
meaning.
      ADJACENT CITY SEWER. Sewer services are available if the public sewer is
located in an easement or public right-of-way on or adjacent to the property on
which any building is located and can be reached by a gravity building sewer of
not more than 200 feet in length constructed in accordance with requirements of
the plumbing code (See
Title 12, Chapter 5 of this code).
      BUILDING SEWER. The sewer line which connects the plumbing of a
residence, building or structure to the city sewer.
      EASEMENT. Easements established by dedication or usage.
      SEWER CONNECTION. The physical connection of the building sewer with the
city owned treatment works/POTW.
   (B)   Sewer use and management ordinance. For purposes of this chapter, the
definitions as set forth in the “sewer use and management ordinance,” and as
hereinafter amended, presently codified at
Title 4, Chapter 7 of this code, are hereby incorporated herein by this
reference as if set forth in full and are hereby made fully applicable to this
chapter.
(Ord. 2064, passed 1-17-1995)
§ 04-05-06 APPLICABILITY OF CHAPTER.
   This chapter shall apply to all property within the corporate limits of the
city and any lot, parcel, premises or building outside of the corporate limits
of the city that is connected to the city owned treatment works/POTW.
(Ord. 2064, passed 1-17-1995)
§ 04-05-07 CONNECTION TO CITY OWNED TREATMENT WORKS/POTW; CONSTRUCTION
STANDARDS.
   (A)   Sewer connection required and penalty.
      (1)   (a)   Every building or structure, including each individual
airport hangar unit even if all airport hangars are contained within the same
building, within the corporate limits of the city shall be separately and
independently connected by a separate building sewer to the POTW where a POTW
sewer line is adjacent to the lot, tract or parcel of land on which the
building or structure stands. Individual service requirements for condominium
projects shall be as per §
11-04-05.
         (b)   No more than one building may be connected to a single service
unless approved by the City Engineer/Public Works Director which approval shall
be an exception not a rule and only based upon overwhelming evidence that such
a connection is the only practical method by which the buildings can be
connected to the POTW and the ownership of the combined service is clearly
designated and all parties are jointly responsible for the maintenance and
operation of the connection, that appropriate easements exist establishing the
right of all buildings to be connected and to use that connection the allowance
of the connection will not impede the city’s ability to collect fees for the
services and does not impede the city’s ability to apply all applicable
ordinances and resolutions regarding the providing of the service and the
establishment of the connection and its maintenance. The City Engineer/Public
Works Director may also deny an application when the capacity of the city’s
POTW might be impaired or there are slope and/or other design issues based upon
reasonable engineering standards and practices regarding such installation as
it pertains to maintenance materials used, diameter of the line, the providing
of cleanouts and the relationship of the buildings to the POTW.
      (2)   No permit shall be issued for the construction of any building or
structure in the city on any lot, tract or parcel of land unless the plans and
specifications show connection to the POTW where a POTW sewer line is adjacent
to the lot, tract or parcel of land on which the building or structure stands.
      (3)   Every building or structure in existence prior to the construction
of a city sewer adjacent to the lot, tract or parcel of land on which the
building or structure stands shall, upon the construction of an adjacent city
sewer, be connected to the city sewer not later than 12 months from the time
the city sewer is certified and accepted, by the City Engineer/Public Works
Director, as being completed and ready to use. The City Council may, based upon
a justified appeal from the owner of the building or structure, extend the time
for connecting to the city sewer. The following may be considered justified
appeals:
         (a)   A claim of financial hardship is presented by the applicant.
Council may allow a time extension to connect of up to 12 months;
         (b)   A point of access into the sewer less than 12 feet deep (as
measured from the invert of the main or service line) is not available. Council
may allow a time extension to connect until such time that a point of access
less than 12 feet deep is available; and
         (c)   A building has a functional site disposal system constructed or
refurbished within the last five years but prior to the time in which sewer
service was available. Council may, upon presentation of satisfactory evidence
as to date of construction by the applicant, allow a time extension to connect
until such time as the constructed or refurbished site disposal system is five
years old.
      (4)   It shall be unlawful to occupy or use any building or structure
that is in violation of this chapter and any violation shall be punishable as a
misdemeanor, and in the circumstance of a continued or immediate health risk,
the city may seek injunctive relief in a court of competent jurisdiction.
   (B)   Standard specification for POTW sewer line connection/permit and
inspection required.
      (1)   The City Engineer/Public Works Director shall duly promulgate
standard specifications for the POTW sewer connection entitled and published as
“Standards and Specifications for City of Caldwell POTW Sewer Connection” which
standards and specifications shall be submitted for approval by the Council and
which copies shall be on file at all times with the Building Inspector and the
City Engineer/Public Works Director.
      (2)   It shall be unlawful for any person, firm, joint venture, trust,
partnership, limited liability company, association or corporation to do, or
cause or permit to be done, whether acting as principal, agent or employee
thereof, any of the following: to uncover, make any connection with, open into,
use, alter and/or disturb any POTW sewer line or other appurtenance thereof,
without first procuring a permit from the City Engineering Department
authorizing such work to be done.
      (3)   Any person, firm, joint venture, partnership, limited liability
company, association or corporation entitled to receive a permit pursuant to
the plumbing regulations of this municipal code of the city shall make
application to the City Engineering Department on the form provided. A
description of the work proposed to be done, its location, ownership, occupancy
and use of the premises shall be given. The City Engineer/Public Works Director
may require plans and specifications and such other information as may be
deemed necessary and pertinent before granting a permit. When it has been
determined that the information furnished by the applicant is in compliance
with this section, the permit shall be issued upon payment of the fees as
hereinafter fixed.
      (4)   Before any permit shall issue, the applicant shall pay to the city
at the time of application, a permit fee for each permit issued which shall
include the costs of inspection and which fee schedule shall be proposed by the
City Engineer/Public Works Director and approved by resolution of the City
Council, and which fee schedule shall not exceed the expense of processing the
permit and performing the inspection.
      (5)   At the time of the issuance of the permit, the Engineering
Department shall notify the applicant at what stage of work the Engineering
Department shall make the inspection. The applicant shall notify the
Engineering Department at said time to make the inspection.
      (6)   All uncovering of connections with openings of, use of, alterations
to or disturbances of the POTW shall be inspected by an agent of the City
Engineering Department to ensure the integrity of the POTW and/or its
appurtenances.
      (7)   It shall be the duty of the permit holder to notify the Engineering
Department at least 24 hours prior to the time of the inspection, exclusive of
Saturdays, Sundays and holidays, that the permittee will be ready for
inspection at a stipulated time. When reinspection is required after the final
inspection because of failure to meet requirements of this section, it shall be
made at a flat charge to be approved by the City Council by resolution not to
exceed the cost of doing the reinspection.
      (8)   Any person, firm, joint venture, trust, partnership, limited
liability company, association or corporation by and through a member,
representative or agent, who shall violate any of the provisions hereof shall
be guilty of a misdemeanor and shall be subject to fine and/or imprisonment, up
to, but not exceeding, the maximum penalties set forth in Idaho Code § 50-302,
as amended.
   (C)   No sewer connections outside city without permit. There shall be no
private sewer lines outside the city connected to the POTW except by permit
issued in accordance with this section.
      (1)   An application for a permit for a private sewer line outside the
city shall be made to the City Clerk who shall forward the same to the City
Engineer/Public Works Director.
      (2)   The City Engineer/Public Works Director shall conduct such inquiry
and obtain such information from the applicant as is necessary to report to the
City Council as to whether or not the permit can be granted and whether or not
the applicant and the parcel to be served qualifies with the criteria under
division (B) above.
      (3)   No permit shall be granted unless the party requesting the
connection complies with the following.
         (a)   If the parcel of real property is legally capable of being
annexed, the applicant must formally request annexation.
         (b)   If the parcel of real property is not legally capable of being
annexed, the applicant must consent and request annexation by a binding
agreement which shall run with the land to which it appertains so that the same
shall operate as a written request for annexation when the property can be
legally annexed.
         (c)   Applicant must consent to be bound and have the real property
bound by agreement to all of the regulations and ordinances of the city
established or thereafter established which govern the operation, maintenance
or expansion of the system, including all provisions related to limitations of
discharge, fees, surcharges, penalties and liabilities to the same extent as if
the parcel were within the corporate boundaries of the city and which agreement
shall be recorded and shall run with the land so long as the connection to the
city’s POTW exists.
         (d)   No connection outside of the city shall be permitted if the
city’s POTW is not meeting the provisions of its (NPDES) discharge permit or if
the waste load of the parcel desiring connection would jeopardize the POTW’s
ability to meet the permit conditions thereof.
         (e)   No parcel shall be permitted to connect to the city’s sanitary
sewer system in the event it would require the city to construct a sewer line
at the expense of the city’s POTW, and all expenses related to the construction
and obtaining of right-of-way shall be borne by the applicant and shall be
constructed in accordance with the specifications and terms and conditions set
forth by the City Engineer/Public Works Director in accordance with the
established specifications and development standards of the city.
         (f)   No parcel shall be connected to the city’s POTW in the event
that such a connection would compromise the ability of the city’s POTW to
provide service to its existing users within the boundaries of the city.
      (4)   The City Engineer/Public Works Director shall submit a report to
the City Council concerning the application with the City Engineer/Public Works
Director’s recommendations to the Council as to whether or not the application
for permit should be granted in accordance with the criteria set forth in
division (C)(3) above.
      (5)   The City Council shall determine whether or not to grant the permit
and may impose such reasonable conditions upon the granting of the permit to
ensure that permit’s compliance with the provisions of division (C)(3) above.
      (6)   Action by the City Council on the application for permit shall be
considered a final action for the city.
   (D)   Construction of sewers by private persons.
      (1)   Sewer construction permit required. Any private person or entity
desiring to construct a sewer main, interceptor or trunk or any other extension
of the POTW shall first obtain from the city a permit for such construction
upon application being filed with and approved by the Public Works Director.
The application shall provide and include engineered and certified plans of the
proposed sewer, the name of the person or entity applying and the location of
the proposed sewer. The design and construction shall be consistent with
relevant sewer master plans and with applicable and/or adopted policies and
standards. The legal description or map of the land or lots to be served by the
sewer, and the approximate cost shall also be provided if cost recovery from
benefiting properties is intended.
      (2)   Certificate of completion. Upon completion, the person constructing
the sewer must file a certificate of completion with the Public Works Director
setting forth the as-built plans of the sewer and certification by the design
engineer of record that construction was completed in conformance with approved
plans and standards. The city shall not accept the operation and maintenance of
said line or facility until it has accepted the same in accordance with a duly
adopted policy regarding dedication of privately constructed facilities.
      (3)   Affidavit of owners participating in cost. If cost recovery from
benefiting properties is intended, the person or entity constructing the sewer
must file with the Public Works Director an affidavit stating the legal
description or map of the lots and the owners thereof who have participated in
the cost of the construction of the sewer and the amount of their
participation.
      (4)   Owners not participating in cost. The person or entity constructing
the sewer may recover the cost of designing and constructing the sewer from
benefited property owners not participating in the cost by entering into an
agreement with the city for the city to collect a proportionate share of the
costs from any such owner connecting subsequent to the date of the agreement
and at the time connection is made. Any agreement must comply with terms
outlined in this section and be approved by City Council. Any fees so collected
shall be accounted for separately, shall be in addition to other approved
connection fees of City Council and to fees outlined in other cost recovery
agreements, and shall be reimbursed at the times as dictated in the agreement.
      (5)   Evidence of expenditures. Any person or entity desiring to recover
costs for the construction of a sewer facility must provide verifiable
evidence, to the satisfaction of the Public Works Director, that the costs were
incurred and paid. The recovery of costs is limited to the total of the
verifiable costs less amounts reimbursed by owners participating in the costs
of construction, as approved by the Public Works Director at the time of the
agreement, and included therein.
      (6)   Sewer already constructed. All persons or entities having
heretofore constructed sewers may file with the Public Works Director a
certificate of completion as provided herein and may enter into an agreement
with the city for recovery of costs under the terms outlined herein. The
provisions of this code for connection of service by owners not participating
in the cost of construction shall thereafter be effective on those sewers
already constructed.
      (7)   Sewer extension. Nothing contained herein shall be construed to
prevent the city, or a person or entity approved by the city, from extending
any sewer main, interceptor or trunk line, or increasing the capacity of any
facility.
      (8)   Time limit for cost recovery. In the recovery of costs of
constructing sewer extensions by private persons, the term of any agreement
shall be limited to a maximum of seven years from the date of completion of
construction of the sewer. The term of any subsequent renewal shall also be
limited to a maximum of seven years. The recovery of costs of constructing
sewer extensions by private persons, by the original agreement and any renewals
to said cost recovery agreement, is limited to 21 years from the date of
completion of construction of the sewer.
      (9)   Other systems. The method of cost recovery described herein may be
applied to drinking water at the discretion of City Council.
(Ord. 2064, passed 1-17-1995; Ord. 2669, passed 2-20-2007; Ord. 2720, passed
12-17-2007; Ord. 2831, passed 5-17-2010)
§ 04-05-08 MAJOR CONTRIBUTING INDUSTRY.
   There is hereby established a category of property owner or sewer user which
shall be known as a significant industrial user which will be subject to
certain regulations and pretreatment responsibilities as indicated in the sewer
use and management ordinance of this code (see
Chapter 7 of this title).
(Ord. 2064, passed 1-17-1995)
§ 04-05-09 FEES, CHARGES AND BILLING ACCOUNTS.
   (A)   Special fees. The city shall have the right to establish special sewer
fees within an identified boundary in the city where POTW sewer facilities have
been constructed or are being maintained that constitute an additional burden
on the city not necessitated by the rest of the city but which specifically
benefit those properties within the identified area. Such fees may include, but
are not limited to, construction of sewer interceptor lines, maintenance of
sewer interceptor lines, the construction of sewage pump stations, maintenance
of sewage pump stations or other facilities that are necessary to provide sewer
service within the identified area.
   (B)   Surcharge. The City Engineer/Public Works Director is hereby
authorized to levy a surcharge on all users of the POTW, in addition to the
rates provided in this chapter, for the purpose of maintenance, operation,
repairs, reconstruction, replacement, extension or expansion of the POTW. Said
surcharge shall be established by rule and regulation promulgated by the City
Engineer/Public Works Director and shall be effective from and after approval
by the City Council.
   (C)   Sewer user charges and fees.
      (1)   The sewer user charge is established for the purpose of equitably
imposing upon all users the costs and expenses of operation, maintenance,
repair and replacement of the POTW. For new connections, the sewer user charge
is to begin when the connection is completed. All owners who derive benefit
from the POTW shall, in return for said benefit, pay user charges. Only the
benefiting property owner, or his or her duly authorized agent, may initiate
service. The procedures for initiating service, disconnecting service, billing
of accounts and processing of delinquent accounts shall be in accordance with
policies adopted by resolution of the City Council. The user charge shall be
based on: the volume and content of effluent discharged into the POTW of the
city; and the costs and expenses of operation, maintenance, repair and
replacement of the POTW, such charges having been determined to be the benefit
derived by each building structure or user being charged.
      (2)   The sewer user charge will be established for each category of use
based on the following classifications.
Waste Strength Category Waste Strength BOD or TSS

      (3)   The user charges and service fees shall be established by the City
Council by resolution duly adopted at a regular Council meeting.
      (4)   The user charges and service fees shall be reviewed annually by the
Treatment Plant Superintendent and the City Engineer/Public Works Director and
revised periodically as required, and the charges and fees provided by this
chapter are hereby levied and assessed against each lot, parcel or tract of
land, or each building, structure or other property having any connection with
the POTW or otherwise discharging sanitary sewage and/or wastewater directly or
indirectly into the POTW.
      (5)   Upon recommendation of the City Engineer/Public Works Director,
billing cycle frequency and due dates for accounts shall be established in the
billing policy, as adopted by resolution of the City Council.
      (6)   Residential user charges shall be based on average water usage
during the three-month consumption period from January through March and shall
be adjusted annually to reflect current use. Properties with three or fewer
dwelling units shall be classified residential.
      (7)   User connections to the POTW not classified as residential shall be
billed based on the actual water metered during the consumption period, unless
approved otherwise by resolution of the City Council.
      (8)   All residential and nonresidential users outside the city limits
shall be billed based on the actual water metered during the consumption period
at two times the user charges for sewer users inside the city limits, unless
approved otherwise by resolution of City Council.
      (9)   The City Engineer/Public Works Director may require users to
install an approved and accessible water meter on private water supplies
discharging into the POTW for determining usage. Installation shall be at the
expense of the property owner. Failure to install a water meter within 60 days
after written notice by the City Engineer/Public Works Director will result in
termination of sewer service at the expense of the property owners.
      (10)   At the initiation or reconnection of service, the city may elect
to collect a security deposit to ensure the ultimate payment of charges and
fees. The procedures for collecting, the amount, the procedures for applying to
delinquent charges and fees and the final disposition of unapplied amounts of
said security deposit shall be in accordance with policies adopted by
resolution of the City Council.
   (D)   Billing accounts.
      (1)   Sewer payments. Payments due the city shall be received and
processed by the Finance Director of the city, in accordance with the state
code.
      (2)   Delinquent accounts. Sewer charges billed shall become delinquent
on the due date. Delinquent accounts shall be processed in accordance with the
billing policy adopted by resolution of the City Council.
      (3)   Service termination. Service shall be terminated and restored in
accordance with the billing policy and rate schedule adopted by resolution of
the City Council.
(Ord. 2064, passed 1-17-1995; Ord. 2465, passed 7-21-2003)
§ 04-05-10 PROHIBITED ACTS.
   (A)   Improper use of system.
      (1)   It shall be unlawful to connect any open gutter, cesspool or privy
vault with any portion of the POTW.
      (2)   No property owner or user shall be allowed or permitted to
discharge sewage into the POTW which shall be deemed deleterious to such system
or which shall endanger the employees, operation or treatment processes of
sewage disposal, or which shall cause encrustation, or shall chemically or
physically attack so as to corrode or erode the sewer lines, treatment
facilities or any other portion of the POTW.
      (3)   Every property owner or user shall be responsible to prevent and
abate any discharge from or upon such owner’s or user’s property into the POTW
which shall be deleterious to the system. The city may send notice of any such
deleterious discharge to the property owner or user by certified or registered
mail. If the property owner or user does not thereafter correct such
deleterious discharge to prevent said discharge within a time specified by the
city, the city or its authorized agents may enter upon the owner’s or user’s
property and make such repairs or do such work as is reasonably necessary to
prevent such deleterious discharge. The property owner or user shall be
responsible for the cost of such work and repairs. If such costs are not paid
by the property owner within 30 days, the costs may be added to and collected
as part of the property owner’s sewer user billing account.
      (4)   Any property owner or user violating the provisions of this section
shall, upon notice by the City Engineer/Public Works Director, immediately
install such preliminary treatment through separators, traps and/or chemical,
physical or biochemical processes as will make and assure that the sewage
contributed from such property or premises will meet the requirements of this
chapter or applicable sections of the sewer use and management ordinance.
   (B)   Use of outside toilets and privies.
      (1)   It shall be unlawful and constitute a misdemeanor for any person to
use or permit the use of, on any premises owned, occupied or used by them, any
outside toilet or privy within the limits of the city.
      (2)   The use of any outside toilet or privy within the limits of the
city is hereby declared to be against public health and to constitute a public
nuisance.
      (3)   Each day this chapter is violated by any person shall constitute a
separate offense.
      (4)   The Building Official may, however, grant permits for the temporary
use of temporary outside toilets, and the operation and use of said toilets
pursuant to said permit shall not be unlawful.
   (C)   Unlawful to discharge unpolluted water to any POTW.
      (1)   It shall be unlawful for any person to discharge or cause to be
discharged any stormwater, surface water, groundwater, roof runoff, subsurface
drainage, uncontaminated cooling water or unpolluted industrial process waters
into the POTW.
      (2)   Any person found to be violating any of these provisions shall be
served with a written notice stating the nature of the violation and providing
a reasonable time limit for satisfactory correction thereof. The offender
shall, within the period of time stated in such notice, permanently cease all
violations.
      (3)   Any person who shall continue any violation beyond the time limit
provided for in division (C)(2) above shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
(Ord. 2064, passed 1-17-1995; Ord. 2889, passed 12-5-2011)
§ 04-05-11 SEVERABILITY.
   Should any section, clause, sentence or provision of this chapter be held
invalid for any reason, such holding or decree shall not be construed as
affecting the validity of any of the remaining portions hereof, it being
declared that the City Council would have adopted the remainder of this
chapter, notwithstanding the invalidity of any such section, clause, sentence
or provision.
(Ord. 2064, passed 1-17-1995)
§ 04-05-12 EFFECTIVE DATE.
   This chapter shall be in full force and effect from and after the passage,
approval and publication according to law of the ordinance codified herein.
(Ord. 2064, passed 1-17-1995)
