§ 11-02-01 PROCEDURES.
   (A)   Procedures; general.
      (1)   Plat approval is required, and a plat shall be drawn for each and
every subdivision of land located within the corporate city limits or the
city’s area of impact, or for proposed subdivision(s) containing land that is
concurrently requesting annexation into the city limits, and shall be submitted
to the Commission and Council as provided below. The city can accept a plat
application for property outside of corporate city limits when there is a
concurrent annexation request submitted.
      (2)   No plat applications shall be accepted for processing if any city
code violations exist on the subject property.
      (3)   No plat shall be filed with the County Recorder until such time as
compliance with the provisions of city code, the state code, certification and
acknowledgment of owners and certification of required agencies has been
completed. All plats shall be recorded in the County Recorder’s office.
      (4)   Preliminary plats submitted for approval shall be addressed through
the public hearing process by the Commission for a recommendation and Council
for a final decision.
      (5)   Final plats submitted for approval shall be addressed by the
Council as an item on the consent agenda.
      (6)   Any application for a preliminary plat, final plat, short plat,
property boundary adjustment, lot line adjustment or total or partial vacation
of an existing subdivision shall be made on forms obtainable from the Planning
and Zoning Department, and the accuracy of the data provided shall be
acknowledged by the applicant.
      (7)   (a)   Building permit applications shall not be accepted for
processing, nor shall any building permit be issued, for any tract or property
or portion of any tract or property contained within a subdivision plat or
within a subdivision plat that has been submitted to the Planning and Zoning
Department for processing, until the final plat for said subdivision plat has
been recorded in the County Recorder’s office.
         (b)   Except that should a parcel have an eligible building permit
available prior to platting, said available building permit may be obtained at
any time during the platting process but shall be held to all requirements of
city code and this title.
      (8)   Any application for any type of plat, planned unit development,
property boundary adjustment, lot line adjustment or plat vacation, and any
related rezone or annexation applications submitted concurrently with any of
the aforementioned applications, shall only be valid for six months from the
date of submittal. Should a final decision not be issued within that time frame
due to the applicant’s continued request for continuation or tabling, the
application(s) shall become null and void. No refunds shall be issued. Should a
final decision not be issued due to the Commission’s or Council’s requests for
continuations, tablings, negotiations or mediation, this requirement shall not
apply.
   (B)   Procedures; preapplication. Any person seeking approval of a
preliminary subdivision plat shall first conduct a neighborhood meeting in
accordance with §
10-03-12 of the zoning regulations.
   (C)   Procedures; application and contents, preliminary plat. The following
procedures shall apply to the filing of a preliminary plat application for
approval of any city subdivision.
      (1)   Application for preliminary plat. Any person desiring to subdivide
within the city shall file with a completed application, completed checklist
and all appropriate fees, with the Planning and Zoning Department on forms
prescribed by the Department, accompanied by such data and information
necessary to assure the fullest presentation of facts, as determined by the
Planning Director. The Director shall have the authority to require any
additional information or data necessary to aid in understanding and reviewing
the request.
      (2)   Proposed subdivision names. Proposed subdivision names shall be
reviewed and approved as an acceptable name by the city.
         (a)   Said name shall not be a duplicate name of any other recorded
subdivision within the county or any of the cities in the county.
         (b)   No changes to an approved subdivision name on a preliminary plat
shall occur unless a request is initiated through the filing of a subdivision
name change request application for administrative staff level review and
approval in accordance with §
11-02-06.
   (D)   Procedures; application and content, final plat. The following
procedures shall apply to the filing of a final plat application for approval
of any city subdivision.
      (1)   Final plat preparation. After the approval of the preliminary plat
by the Council, the applicant may cause the subdivision, or any part thereof,
to be surveyed and a final plat prepared in general accordance with the
preliminary plat as approved, notwithstanding any items on the preliminary plat
that did not meet city code and were not approved as exceptions.
      (2)   Acceptance of a final plat application. Final plat applications,
after having been prepared in accordance with state code requirements and the
provisions set forth herein, shall be submitted to the Planning and Zoning
Department in accordance with the following.
         (a)   Final plat applications shall be submitted to the Planning and
Zoning Department at the same time the application for review of construction
drawings has been submitted to the Engineering Department.
         (b)   In making application for a final plat, the applicant shall file
a completed final plat application, the number of copies of the final plat
required, by size as specified, a completed checklist and all appropriate fees
with the Planning and Zoning Department on forms prescribed by the Department,
accompanied by such data and information necessary to assure the fullest
presentation of facts, as determined by the Planning Director. The Director
shall have the authority to require any additional information or data
necessary to aid in understanding and reviewing the request. The submittal date
of all final plats and applications will be based on the date in which all
required documents have been received and reviewed by the city and all required
fees have been paid.
         (c)   Final plats shall be reviewed and heard by City Council as
outlined in §
11-02-03(B).
   (E)   Procedures; application and content, short plat.
      (1)   A subdivision application for property may be processed as a short
plat if all of the following exist:
         (a)   The proposed subdivision does not exceed four buildable lots;
         (b)   No right-of-way dedication is necessary as required by city
code;
         (c)   No installation of public improvements or infrastructure
improvements is necessary as required by city code;
         (d)   No street widening is necessary as required by city code; and
         (e)   There are no impacts on the health, safety or general welfare of
the city and the subdivision is in the best interest of the city.
      (2)   If the plat is a condominium plat application, it may be processed
as a short plat, regardless of the number of buildable lots and provided all
buildings have approved building permits; no right-of-way dedication is
necessary; no installation of public improvements or infrastructure
improvements is necessary; no street widening is necessary; and there are no
impacts on the health, safety or general welfare of the city and the
subdivision is in the best interest of the city.
      (3)   Contents for short plats shall follow preliminary and final plat
procedures as listed in this chapter, except that both the preliminary and
final plat shall be submitted concurrently rather than separately.
      (4)   Review and hearings for short plats shall be approved by City
Council with recommendation from Planning and Zoning and/or the City Engineer.
The preliminary and final plat shall be heard concurrently rather than
separately.
(Ord. 2768, passed 4-20-2009; Ord. 2811, passed 11-2-2009; Ord. 3576, passed 3-
19-2024)
§ 11-02-02 PHASED SUBDIVISIONS.
   The following provisions apply to phased subdivisions.
   (A)   Subdivisions with more than one phase are permitted provided the
proposed subdivision has a minimum total of 20 or more buildable lots if
residential, or two or more buildable lots if anything other than residential.
      (1)   Each phase shall consist of a minimum number of buildable lots,
whichever is the greatest, of: 20 buildable lots if residential or two
buildable lots if anything other than residential; or 10% of the total
buildable lots for the entire project.
      (2)   A phasing plan shall be submitted with the preliminary plat
application showing the total number of phases, total number of buildable lots
for the entire project and the total number of buildable lots in each phase.
   (B)   The subdivider may file and obtain acceptance of successive final
plats for continuous segments of the approved preliminary plat without
reapplication for preliminary plat approval, provided that:
      (1)   The final plat application for subsequent phases shall not be heard
by City Council until Council approval is received for the previous phase;
      (2)   The final plat for subsequent phases is recorded in successive
intervals of not more than two years each, as measured from the date of
recordation of the prior phase final plat; and
      (3)   The city code and any subsequent ordinance amendments as adopted by
the city before, during or after preliminary plat approval, is followed in all
design, engineering plans, construction and final plats for all phases, with
the exception of lot sizes, lot dimensions, setbacks, number of lots and any
exceptions approved at the time of preliminary platting, which shall remain as
indicated in the preliminary plat order of decision and/or development
agreement.
   (C)   In the event the approved phasing plan needs to be modified by adding
additional phases or increasing or decreasing the number of buildable lots
within a phase, a modified phasing plan shall be submitted to the Planning and
Zoning Department for administrative approval by the Planning and Zoning
Department in consultation with the Engineering Department.
(Ord. 3673, passed 4-21-2025)
§ 11-02-03 REVIEW AND HEARINGS.
   (A)   Preliminary plat review and hearings.
      (1)   City department review. The Planning and Zoning Department shall
transmit one copy of the application and preliminary plat to all applicable
city departments for review and comments.
      (2)   Public agency review. The Planning and Zoning Department shall
notify all political subdivisions providing services within the planning
jurisdiction, including school districts, in accordance with Idaho Code Title
67, Chapter 65 and §
10-03-12 of the zoning regulations.
      (3)   Agencies to receive preliminary plat. Some of the agencies which
receive copies of the preliminary plat may be as follows:
         (a)   School districts;
         (b)   Transportation agencies and highway districts;
         (c)   Utility, irrigation and drainage companies or districts;
         (d)   County, municipal, state and federal agencies; and
         (e)   Other agencies as determined by the Planning and Zoning
Department.
      (4)   Staff report. A staff report shall be prepared by the Planning and
Zoning Department and submitted to the applicant prior to the meeting at which
the preliminary plat is to be considered. The staff report shall, at a minimum,
list or summarize all agency and city department responses as well as provide a
comprehensive plan analysis, an analysis of compliance with city code and staff
recommended conditions.
      (5)   Preliminary plat hearings.
         (a)   Review. Once all departments have completed their review of the
preliminary plat, and after meeting all the requirements for public noticing in
accordance with this title, the Planning and Zoning Department shall place the
request for preliminary plat approval on the first available agenda for the
Commission to be heard through the public hearing process as outlined in §
10-03-12 of the zoning regulations.
         (b)   Commission action. The Commission shall recommend to the Council
approval, conditional approval or denial of the preliminary plat.
         (c)   Following an action of the Commission. The Planning and Zoning
Department shall place the request for preliminary plat approval on the
Council’s agenda to be heard through the public hearing process as outlined in
§
10-03-12 of the zoning regulations, once the Department has determined all
conditions that were required to be met prior to being heard by City Council,
have in fact been satisfied.
         (d)   City Council action. The City Council, prior to approving a
preliminary plat request, shall find and conclude the requests have met the
criteria identified below and shall make the express findings of such:
            1.   The plat is in compliance with city code;
            2.   The plat is consistent with the city comprehensive plan;
            3.   Public services and utilities are available or can be made
available and are adequate to accommodate the proposed subdivision;
            4.   The plat is consistent with the city transportation master
plan; and
            5.   The subdivision preserves natural, scenic or historic features
on the site that is being developed, if applicable.
   (B)   Final plat review and hearing.
      (1)   City department review. The Planning and Zoning Department shall
transmit one copy of the application and final plat to all applicable city
departments for review and comment.
      (2)   Public agency noticing. The Planning and Zoning Department shall
notify all political subdivisions providing services within the planning
jurisdiction, including school districts who will be impacted by any changes
that have been proposed from what was originally approved on the preliminary
plat.
      (3)   Order of decision. A final plat order of decision shall be prepared
by the Planning and Zoning Department which shall, at a minimum, list or
summarize all agency and city department responses as well as provide an
analysis of general compliance with the approved preliminary plat and
applicable development agreements and conditions of approval from applicable
orders of decision, as well as list recommended conditions of approval for the
final plat.
      (4)   Final plat approval, City Council.
         (a)   Upon completion of the final plat review, the Planning and
Zoning Department may thereafter place the final plat on the Council consent
agenda for consideration at the next regular meeting, along with the request
for dedication of sanitary sewer and domestic water facilities.
         (b)   Final plats shall not be considered by Council until
construction drawings have been reviewed and approved, and the Planning and
Zoning Department, in consultation with the Engineering Department, has
determined the final plat is compliant with city code as well as with the
approved preliminary plat.
         (c)   Approval, with conditions, of the final plat by Council shall be
dependent upon compliance with the city code and compliance with the approved
preliminary plat.
      (5)   Final plat signatures. The final plat will not be considered for
final signature until all of the following has been met, in addition to
compliance with all conditions of approval as specified within the signed
findings of fact, conclusions of law and order of decision for the final plat.
         (a)   All required improvements, infrastructure, public utilities,
public improvements and the like have been installed and conditions of approval
have been met and inspected and approved by the city, including all record
drawing requirements, submittal of engineer of record inspection logs,
submittal of the engineer of record certification and receipt of the dedication
request and a memo or e-mail from the Engineering Department has been issued
stating as much.
         (b)   The Engineering Department has approved the amount of the
financial guarantee as outlined in §
11-04-07(A) for required improvements and conditions of approval that have yet
to be completed and all of the following items have been completed by the
developer and inspected and approved by the Engineering Department and a memo
or e-mail from the Engineering Department has been issued stating as much:
            1.   Construction of the domestic water system, including
successful pressure and bacteria tests by the developer and inspection and
approval by the city;
            2.   Construction of the sanitary sewer system, including
successful pressure test, television camera inspection, completion of all work
within the base of the manholes by the developer and inspection and approval by
the city;
            3.   Construction of an all-weather road system by the developer
and inspection and approval by the city;
            4.   Installation of street signs by the developer and inspection
and approval by the City Engineer in consultation with the Fire Marshal;
            5.   Request by developer for dedication of all sanitary sewer and
domestic water facilities and submittal of applicable documentation as required
by the Engineering Department to process said request; and
            6.   Construction and testing of the irrigation system by the
developer and inspection and approval by the city, where applicable. Further,
the city must receive documentation requesting that the system be annexed into
the city municipal irrigation district if annexation is applicable. All
applicable fees must be submitted with the annexation request. Under
circumstances where seasonal restrictions prevent the total completion of said
irrigation system, the City Engineer may allow, at his or her sole discretion,
those portions of said system under seasonal restriction to be deferred until
the first available construction window. Any deferred portions shall be
included in the financial guarantee.
         (c)   The final plat shall not be signed by the City Engineer nor
released by the City Engineer for recording until the city has received the
financial guarantee in compliance with this title and Council has approved the
final plat.
      (6)   Final plat recording.
         (a)   A public pathway access easement (if applicable) must be
recorded and the instrument number included on the final recorded plat.
         (b)   Upon recordation of the final plat, all recorded subdivisions
shall be known and referred to by the city approved subdivision name, in all
permanent or temporary signage physically located on or near the location of
the subdivision and on all deeds and legal documents. This requirement shall
continue through the development of each phase of the subdivision and shall
survive completion of the subdivision unless a request is initiated through the
filing of a subdivision name change request application in accordance with §
11-02-06. No alternative, abbreviated or incomplete subdivision names, other
than the complete name identified in the recorded final plat, shall be
recognized by the city, except that a variation in the subdivision name
required by this title may be permitted for parcels within the subdivision that
are being developed solely for commercial or multi-family commercial
apartments, as approved by the city, and may be designed and constructed as
their own separate phases which do not have to follow the subdivision phasing
sequencing required by this title.
(Ord. 2768, passed 4-20-2009; Ord. 2811, passed 11-2-2009; Ord. 2983, passed
12-15-2014; Ord. 3328, passed 5-3-2021; Ord. 3576, passed 3-19-2024; Ord. 3673,
passed 4-21-2025)
§ 11-02-04 PRELIMINARY PLAT EXPIRATIONS, TIME EXTENSIONS AND RENEWALS.
   (A)   Plat expirations.
      (1)   Final plats must be submitted for approval within 24 months of the
date of signature on the approving order of decision for the preliminary plat.
      (2)   Final plats must be recorded for a single-phase development or for
the first phase of a multi-phase development within 24 months of City Council
approval of the final plat. For phased subdivisions, see §
11-02-02.
      (3)   The plat (final plat) must be recorded within 24 months of the date
of signature on the approving order of decision.
   (B)   Preliminary and/or final plat time extensions.
      (1)   Prior to the expiration date of a plat, an applicant may file for
an administrative time extension, by filing a completed application, checklist
and all appropriate fees, with the Planning and Zoning Department on forms
prescribed by the Department, accompanied by such data and information
necessary to assure the fullest presentation of facts, as determined by the
Planning Director. The Director shall have the authority to require any
additional information or data necessary to aid in understanding and reviewing
the request submitting an application to the Planning and Zoning Department.
      (2)   Time extensions of up to 24 months may be authorized by the
Planning and Zoning Director and City Engineer following applicant’s submittal
of an application. There shall be no limit to the number of time extensions
that may be approved so long as the plat is still valid and in conformance with
the approval criteria within division (B)(4) below.
      (3)   If an administrative time extension is denied, the applicant may
appeal the decision to the Council and follow the process as outlined in §
10-03-12 of the zoning regulations.
      (4)   Extension requests for plats shall be approved based upon the
following.
         (a)   The plat, as previously approved, is still in the best interests
of the safety, health and general welfare of the city.
         (b)   There have been no significant changes to the city code between
the date of plat approval and the application date of the time extension
request that would require substantial modifications.
         (c)   Any modification to the layout and design of the originally
approved plat are minimal.
         (d)   The plat still conforms with new or amended development master
plans, including, but not limited to, public facilities plans, pathways and
bike routes plans, parks and recreation master plans.
         (e)   The plat is still active and valid. If the plat is expired, the
applicant shall apply for a renewal in conjunction with the request for a time
extension and pay all the applicable fees for such renewal. Renewals will only
be granted if the plat meets the requirements of division (C) below.
         (f)   There are no outstanding city code violations on the subject
property or properties, to include any land use violations.
      (5)   The extension of a subdivision plat automatically extends the
approvals of all other applications associated with the plat such as a planned
unit development and special use permit.
   (C)   Plat renewals.
      (1)   One plat renewal of up to 18 months may be authorized by the
Planning and Zoning Director and City Engineer for all expired preliminary plat
approvals. No preliminary plat renewal shall be granted if there are any
outstanding city code violations on the subject property. The Planning and
Zoning Director and City Engineer shall consider approval of said renewal in
accordance with the criteria listed in division (B)(4) above.
      (2)   No renewal shall be granted for any plat that has been expired for
a period of time exceeding 12 months (if no development has occurred), or for a
period of time exceeding 24 months (if development has occurred), regardless of
when the original date of approval occurred for the preliminary plat.
(Ord. 3576, passed 3-19-2024; Ord. 3673, passed 4-21-2025)
§ 11-02-05 PLAT AMENDMENTS AND CORRECTIONS.
   (A)   Preliminary plat amendments. Changes to an approved preliminary plat
made prior to final plat approval and recording and incorporated within the
final plat design shall not require rehearing of the original preliminary plat
by the Planning and Zoning Commission or by City Council if the proposed design
change(s) does not:
      (1)   Reduce the lot size below the minimum approved on the preliminary
plat entitlement;
      (2)   Increase the number of buildable lots by more than 10% of the
original request, provided the number of dwelling units does not increase;
      (3)   Substantially alter the alignment of the subdivision’s ingress/
egress access points and/or connectivity of the subdivision’s roadway network
to a degree that would necessitate changes to the traffic impact study, or
adversely impact the original engineering conditions for the project;
      (4)   Substantially re-align the internal street network such that the
subdivision is effectively a new project, as determined by the Director or City
Engineer;
      (5)   Increase the exterior boundaries of the preliminary plat as already
approved;
      (6)   Reduce the square footage of common areas or the number of public
amenities below the levels approved through the public hearing process. Minor
modifications to the types and locations of amenities may be permitted as
determined by the Director; and
      (7)   Violate the terms of a development agreement.
   (B)   Plat corrections. Affidavits of correction prepared, signed and
stamped by a professional land surveyor which fully describes each error and
each correction to be made, by specific reference to the approved plat, may be
used to correct minor errors on a previously approved final plat, including,
but not limited to:
      (1)   Typographical and spelling errors or transpositions;
      (2)   Minor changes to mapping;
      (3)   Incorrect seal;
      (4)   Incorrect dates;
      (5)   Monumentation incorrectly noted or drawn;
      (6)   Incorrect or missing interior dimensions on the drawing;
      (7)   Missing or incorrectly displayed arrows, graphic scales or symbols;
      (8)   Changes to the names of streets or the name of the existing plat;
and
      (9)   Changes to the numbering scheme used for lots and/or blocks.
(Ord. 3576, passed 3-19-2024; Ord. 3673, passed 4-21-2025)
§ 11-02-06 CHANGES TO AN APPROVED SUBDIVISION NAME.
   No changes to an approved subdivision name shall occur unless a request is
initiated through the filing of an application for a subdivision name change
request and subsequently reviewed and approved by the Mapping and Planning and
Zoning Department, at an administrative staff level. In making application, the
applicant shall file a completed application with the Planning and Zoning
Department on forms prescribed by the Department accompanied by such data and
information necessary to assure the fullest presentation of facts, as
determined by the Planning Director.
   (A)   Name change requests; prior to final plat submission. If approved, an
amended preliminary plat will need to be submitted to the Planning and Zoning
Department with the reflected subdivision name change prior to the approval of
construction drawings. All construction drawings and final subdivision plats
shall reflect the new approved subdivision name.
   (B)   Name change requests; prior to final plat recording. If approved,
amended final plat drawings and Mylars will need to be submitted to the
Planning and Zoning Department with the reflected subdivision name change prior
to signature of the final plat.
   (C)   Name change requests; after final plat recording. If approved, an
amended final plat drawing indicating the new subdivision name or an affidavit
of correction indicating that the plat is otherwise known as “insert the new
approved subdivision name,” shall be recorded at the County Recorder’s office.
Once the plat or affidavit is recorded, a copy of the recorded plat or
affidavit shall be provided to the Planning and Zoning Department.
   (D)   Violation. Owners and developers acting in violation of this section
shall be subject to the administrative citation process outlined in §
10-03-10 of the zoning regulations.
(Ord. 3576, passed 3-19-2024)
CHAPTER 3: DESIGN AND CONSTRUCTION STANDARDS AND REQUIREMENTS
Section
   
11-03-01   General details
   
11-03-02   Street requirements
   
11-03-03   Block requirements
   
11-03-04   Lot requirements
   
11-03-05   Easement requirements
§ 11-03-01 GENERAL DETAILS.
   (A)   Conform to standards. Every phase of all subdivisions and planned unit
developments shall conform to the standards of the adopted comprehensive plan,
the zoning regulations of the city, city code as well as all subsequent adopted
updates and amendments to city code unless exceptions were granted by Council
and listed in the order of decision for the preliminary plat and/or development
agreement; also excepting lot sizes, lot dimensions, setbacks and number of
lots which shall remain as indicated in the preliminary order of decision and/
or development agreement.
   (B)   Specifications and/or standards adopted. The city has adopted
specifications and details of the “Idaho Standards for Public Works
Construction” (hereinafter referred to as ISPWC) as standards for construction
and design within the impact area and city limits and shall adopt later
editions of ISPWC by resolution. These standards are augmented by general
addenda, including city supplemental specifications (hereinafter referred to as
CSS), approved by resolution of the Council as necessary, to ensure uniform
material selection and construction practice for those items specific to the
city.
(Ord. 2768, passed 4-20-2009)
§ 11-03-02 STREET REQUIREMENTS.
   (A)   Design and construction conformance. The design and construction of
all streets and alleys shall conform to requirements of the city transportation
master plan, “Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices” (hereinafter referred
to as MUTCD), ISPWC and CSS.
   (B)   Partial street dedications. Partial street dedications shall not be
permitted unless the street forms the boundary of the property being
subdivided, the adjacent property is not under common ownership, or the street
is anticipated to be a through street upon development of adjacent properties.
All partial street dedications shall require construction of partial street
sections of no less than 26 feet in width from centerline to back of curb that
meet the requirements of the city transportation master plan, ISPWC and CSS.
When the property abutting the partial street develops, the owner of that
property shall be required to complete the construction of the street section,
mirroring the street section and right-of-way of the already constructed
original portion, including dedication of any additional right-of-way required
by the city.
   (C)   Dead end and stub streets. Dead end streets are prohibited. Stub
streets may be allowed when said stub street and its extension is shown on the
city transportation master plan or when, in the opinion of the Planning and
Zoning Director and City Engineer, the future extension of said stub street is
feasible and necessary to the proper development of the street pattern. All
stub streets authorized by this title shall be clearly marked by signage at the
end of the stub street to indicate that such street is planned to be extended
in the future.
   (D)   Continuation of existing street. Proposed streets which are a
continuation of an existing street shall be given the same name as the existing
street, except that the proposed street shall carry the correct street
designation (street, drive, avenue, way and the like) even though the existing
street designation may be incorrect.
   (E)   Street naming. All street naming shall be in accordance with
Title 5 of this code.
   (F)   Frontage streets and cross access. Where a subdivision/development
abuts or contains an existing or proposed arterial street, railroad or limited
access highway, the City Engineer may require frontage streets, or such other
treatment for the appropriate use of the tract. Cross access on the subject
property in the absence of frontage streets along higher level arterials in
commercial development shall be required to provide continuous public cross
access to both the subject property and adjacent development.
   (G)   Connectivity. A minimum of one street connection for vehicular
connectivity shall be provided to all adjacent properties for all subdivisions/
developments, at appropriate locations as determined by the Engineering
Department, Fire Department and Planning and Zoning Department, excepting that
this condition may be waived by the Engineering Department and Planning and
Zoning Department as a joint decision, or by Council if topography, geography,
dimensions or size of the subdivision/development are such that no connectivity
is warranted or feasible. Additionally, in the event an adjacent property has
already developed and did not have provision for connectivity, the connectivity
requirement may be waived for the new project in that specific direction only.
   (H)   Loop streets. Loop streets shall be limited to a maximum length of 600
feet measured along the centerline of the street from the centerline
intersection to centerline intersection. Loop streets are permitted on a case-
by-case basis and are subject to review and approval by both the Fire
Department and the Engineering Department. The Fire Department discourages the
use of loop streets.
   (I)   Emergency service vehicle accessibility. The following street
distances, configurations, specifications and related items are required to
satisfy accessibility to subdivisions and planned unit developments by
emergency services vehicles.
      (1)   A cul-de-sac, court or similar type street may be permitted
provided the maximum length for such street shall not exceed 600 feet as
measured from the centerline intersection of such street and the street from
which such street takes access to the center of the cul-de-sac turnaround.
      (2)   Cul-de-sac turnarounds must meet Fire Department approval as
referenced in International Fire Code Appendix D.
      (3)   The length of any driveway, regardless of use or zone, shall not
exceed 150 feet unless the subdivider has received Fire Department approval.
      (4)   Minimum driveway widths shall be 20 feet. Landscaping shall be
installed so as to protect a clear height of 13 feet six inches within the
required 20-foot width.
      (5)   (a)   Primary and emergency access shall be required as approved by
the Fire Department, which may approve other mitigation in lieu of emergency
access, for all subdivisions and planned unit developments.
         (b)   If the development contemplates emergency access by means of
streets to be constructed in future phases and provides interim emergency
access improved to Fire Department standards for temporary access over a
temporary emergency access easement which is irrevocable until such future
streets are dedicated and constructed, the emergency access requirement shall
be considered to be met.
      (6)   Primary and emergency accesses, for Fire Department purposes, shall
be constructed to the following minimum standards (which do not preclude more
restrictive minimum standards as set forth by the Engineering Department or
another state or federal agency).
         (a)   Minimum width of 20 feet with a minimum inside turning radius of
28 feet, minimum outside turning radius of 48 feet and maximum grade of 10%.
         (b)   Surface shall be improved with an all-weather surface meeting
the Fire Department standards and capable of supporting two-axled vehicles
weighing 80,000 pounds.
         (c)   Emergency accesses for emergency purposes only shall not be open
to general vehicular travel and shall be provided with removable bollards,
gates or other means approved by the Fire Department to restrict general
vehicular access. Such emergency accesses may serve as pedestrian and bicycle
pathways.
         (d)   Applicant shall construct required emergency accesses prior to
submittal of the final plat application.
         (e)   Emergency access easements located within the plat shall be
delineated on the face of the final plat. The applicant shall provide covenants
for the maintenance of any emergency access by a homeowners’ or business
owners’ association or other as approved by the Fire Department.
         (f)   Emergency access easements located outside the plat shall be by
permanent recorded easements which shall contain covenants for maintenance
acceptable to the Fire Department. Said easements shall be recorded and a copy
submitted with the final plat application along with a draft of said covenants.
   (J)   Minimum right-of-way widths. Minimum required right-of-way widths as
per CSS.
   (K)   Minimum street widths and sections. Minimum street widths and street
sections as per CSS.
   (L)   Street grades. Street grades shall be as per CSS.
   (M)   Street and approach design and construction. All curves, street
alignments, approach spacing, street design and construction and approach
design and construction shall be as per CSS, city transportation master plan
and city access control standards for state administered highways and city
administered surface streets.
   (N)   Common driveways.
      (1)   (a)   Common driveways shall be a minimum of 24 feet in width,
shall meet all applicable Fire Code requirements and shall serve no more than
six residential units and no more than three commercial or industrial lots.
         (b)   Where city owned utilities are constructed within the common
driveway, the driveway shall be constructed with an asphaltic concrete surface;
Portland cement is not permitted as the surface material. The driveway, at a
minimum, shall match the width of any required utility easements.
      (2)   Common driveways shall be a maximum of 150 feet in length.
      (3)   Common driveways shall be paved with a surface with the capability
of supporting two-axled vehicles and fire equipment, at a minimum 75,000
pounds.
      (4)   Unless limited by a significant geographical feature, or separated
by a minimum five-foot-wide landscaped common lot, all lots that abut a common
driveway shall take access from the driveway not the public street.
      (5)   Common driveways shall be straight or provide a minimum 28-foot
inside and 48-foot outside turning radius.
      (6)   For any lots using a common driveway, the setbacks, dimensioned
building envelope and orientation of the lots and structures to the driveway
shall be shown on the preliminary plat for those lots and as an exhibit with
the final plat application.
      (7)   Common driveways shall not require curb, gutter or sidewalks on
either side of the length of the common driveway by default, but they may be
required on one side of a common driveway as a condition of development.
      (8)   Common driveways shall be identified and platted as common lots to
be owned and maintained by a homeowners’ or business owners’ association or as
perpetual ingress-egress easements to be maintained by a homeowners’ or
business owners’ association and shall be so indicated by note on the final
plat.
      (9)   No parking shall be permitted on common driveways.
      (10)   The public street frontage requirement for lots utilizing a common
driveway is not applicable. Lots utilizing a common driveway shall be addressed
pursuant to §
05-07-05.
   (O)   Private streets.
      (1)   Where permitted. Private streets may only be permitted as described
herein:
         (a)   Within developments that are wholly commercial or industrial in
use or that are a mixture of commercial and industrial; and
         (b)   Within multi-family developments as described herein:
            1.   Within a multi-family development under single ownership and
not considered a subdivision as defined within this code;
            2.   Within a mixed-use development which has a portion of the
development being developed as multi-family. In this scenario, private streets
may only be allowed within the area being developed as multi-family; and
            3.   Within a subdivided multi-family project, or multi-family
portion of a mixed-use development. Subdivider shall establish an agreement
specifying that the private streets are to be owned and maintained by the
homeowners’ association. A copy of said agreement shall be provided to the
city.
      (2)   General construction and design requirements.
         (a)   All private street construction shall be in accordance with city
supplemental specifications structural standards for base course and asphaltic
concrete mat thickness. The design shall be prepared and certified by a
registered professional engineer.
         (b)   The minimum width of private streets shall be 24 feet.
         (c)   Curbs, gutter and sidewalks shall not be required unless
specifically required by Council.
         (d)   Maintenance of private streets shall take place through a
business owners’ association and shall be so noted on a final plat.
         (e)   Private streets shall be designated as either perpetual
easements or common lots and shall be platted as one or the other.
         (f)   Private streets shall be labeled “private street” within the
area of the private street on the final plat.
         (g)   It shall be noted on the final plat that private streets are not
the responsibility of the city and should landowners ever desire city
maintenance of said streets, said private streets would have to be brought up
to city standards which would include, at a minimum, curb, gutter, asphalt
paving, subsurfacing, sidewalk and storm drainage, all inspected and accepted
by the city.
         (h)   It shall be noted on the final plat that, if there are any
utilities located within the private streets, a utility easement shall be
platted and any required maintenance or repair to the utility within the
utility easement shall take place regardless of any potential damage or
destruction to the street as a consequence of the utility maintenance or repair
and repair or replacement shall not be the responsibility of the utility or the
city nor shall the utility or the city be held liable for any damage to the
street due to utility maintenance or repair.
(Ord. 2768, passed 4-20-2009; Ord. 2811, passed 11-2-2009; Ord. 3379, passed
12-20-2021; Ord. 3576, passed 3-19-2024; Ord. 3673, passed 4-21-2025)
§ 11-03-03 BLOCK REQUIREMENTS.
   (A)   Block numbers shall be designated as required by the state code.
   (B)   Block lengths shall not exceed 600 feet as measured along the street
centerline from centerline intersection to centerline intersection in all
subdivisions that are wholly or partially residential in use excepting the
following.
      (1)   In the RS-1 and RS-2 Zoning Districts, block lengths shall not
exceed 1,200 feet as measured along the street centerline from centerline
intersection to centerline intersection.
      (2)   Commercial and industrial subdivisions shall not have a maximum
block length.
      (3)   The project is a planned unit development and an exception from the
maximum block length has been requested and granted, as part of the
application.
(Ord. 2768, passed 4-20-2009)
§ 11-03-04 LOT REQUIREMENTS.
   (A)   Lot size or area, width, frontage and minimum setback lines for
buildable lots shall comply with the minimum requirements of the zoning
regulations of the city as stated in
Title 10 of this code, unless stated otherwise in this title.
   (B)   Double frontage lots are prohibited. Installation of a minimum five-
foot-wide street landscape buffer, said buffer complying with street landscape
buffer requirements, except width, as stated in
Title 10 of this code, and designated as a common lot, shall serve to eliminate
double frontage.
   (C)   No individual buildable lot or individual common lot shall have direct
access to or from any classified street, regardless of zoning district or use.
There is no exception to this, unless the lot is for a school or is commercial
or industrial in zone or use, in which case, the City Engineer shall consider
direct access on a case-by-case basis taking into account the city
transportation master plan, the traffic impact study and public safety.
   (D)   Flag lots, as herein defined, are permitted provided all other
provisions of city code are met. Only one primary dwelling or building is
permitted per flag lot, excluding accessory buildings.
   (E)   Alley loaded lots are permitted as follows:
      (1)   An alley with a minimum width of 24 feet, and built to city
specifications with a half width street section of ten feet of paving from
centerline to a two-foot width of rolled curb and gutter, is provided at the
rear of such lots to provide direct lot access. Sidewalks are not required. The
alley shall be the only means allowed for access;
      (2)   “No parking” signage is placed on both sides of the alley and no
parking is ever allowed. Additionally, curbing shall either be painted red or
red dye shall be installed in the concrete to further prohibit parking;
      (3)   Direct lot access to any classified street is prohibited and a note
shall be placed on the final plat stating such;
      (4)   Alley loaded lots, as herein outlined and permitted, shall not be
considered double frontage lots for purposes of this title; and
      (5)   Alley loaded lots and the “no parking” requirement along the alley
do not preclude the satisfaction of all city code parking requirements. On
street parking spaces that are lost due to the “no parking” requirement along
the alley shall be provided elsewhere in the project within at least 600 feet
of the block in which the alley loaded lots are located.
(Ord. 2768, passed 4-20-2009)
§ 11-03-05 EASEMENT REQUIREMENTS.
   (A)   A general utility, irrigation and drainage easement of a minimum ten
feet in width is required along all front and rear lot lines and shall be shown
and dedicated as such on the final plat.
   (B)   In certain instances as required by the City Engineer, a general
utility, irrigation and drainage easement of a minimum five feet in width shall
be required along interior lot lines and shall be shown and dedicated as such
on the final plat.
   (C)   All existing recorded easements, with width, use, dimensions and
bearings, shall be shown on final plats along with the applicable instrument
numbers. All proposed easements, with width, use, dimensions and bearings,
shall be shown on final plats.
   (D)   All utility lines on and within the boundaries of a subdivision shall
be underground.
(Ord. 2768, passed 4-20-2009; Ord. 2811, passed 11-2-2009)

11-04-07   Financial guarantees
§ 11-04-01 PURPOSE.
   (A)   Define the responsibility of the subdivider in the planning, design,
construction, inspection and financing of required improvements;
   (B)   Establish procedures for review and approval of engineering plans and
subsequent construction and inspection process; and
   (C)   Outline minimum acceptable standards for improvements, including, but
not limited to, streets, curbs, gutters, sidewalks, alleys, easements, other
facilities required as a condition to plat approval.
(Ord. 2768, passed 4-20-2009)
§ 11-04-02 SUBDIVIDER’S RESPONSIBILITY.
   (A)   The subdivider, at his or her expense, has the responsibility of
designing, constructing and having inspected and approved all required
improvements to city specifications and standards.
   (B)   The subdivider has the responsibility of maintaining the subdivision
property in a nuisance free manner until such time that the subdivision is
turned over to a homeowners’ or business owners’ association. Maintenance shall
include the mowing of all weeds (said mowing to take place at least monthly
within the months of April, May, June, July, August, September and October)
within the subdivision boundaries and the immediate removal of noxious weeds
when they are identified, as well as the immediate removal of all loose, dead
and/or dying plant material which would include the mowed weed material. All
appropriate dust abatement procedures shall be applied as necessary for dust
mitigation during the entire development and construction process until build
out is complete, including watering of unpaved surfaces in regular use and the
application of dust inhibitors.
   (C)   At the time of development a “rules and regulations” sign shall be
posted and maintained at the entryways to the project until it is fully
developed and build out is complete. The signs would be intended for
subcontractors performing work and should include:
      (1)   No dogs;
      (2)   No loud music;
      (3)   No alcohol or drugs;
      (4)   No abusive language;
      (5)   Disposal of personal trash and site debris;
      (6)   Daily cleanup of any mud and/or dirt that is deposited from the
construction parcel onto streets;
      (7)   Installation of a temporary construction fence that would keep
debris from being blown off-site by the wind; and
      (8)   No burning of construction or other debris on the property.
   (D)   Coordinate with the United States Postal Office to determine the best
location for mailbox placement prior to preliminary plat approval. Mailbox
placement shall not be within any vision triangle area.
   (E)   In subdivisions containing residential uses, coordinate with the local
school bus company to determine a detailed school bus stop plan and layout. A
letter shall be provided to the Planning and Zoning Department from the local
school bus company, prior to preliminary plat approval, indicating said bus
company’s approval of said detailed school bus stop plan and layout.
(Ord. 2768, passed 4-20-2009; Ord. 2811, passed 11-2-2009)
§ 11-04-03 ENGINEERING PLANS.
   (A)   The subdivider shall retain a professional engineer, currently
licensed in the state, to prepare and submit a complete set of engineering
plans, satisfactory to the City Engineer, for construction of required
improvements.
   (B)   Engineering plans shall be based on conditions of approval as outlined
in the order of decision related to the preliminary plat, and any development
agreement pertinent to the subject property, as well as city code and this
title.
   (C)   Engineering plans shall further be based on the approved preliminary
plat as modified by the preliminary plat order of decision and/or development
agreement, notwithstanding any items on the approved preliminary plat not
consistent with city code that were not specifically addressed and approved as
an exception in the order of decision and/or development agreement.
   (D)   Engineering plans shall be approved for construction by the
Engineering Department prior to commencement of any construction. Approval
shall be based upon the preliminary plat order of decision and/or development
agreement, city code, this title, the approved preliminary plat as modified by
the preliminary plat order of decision and/or development agreement and any
exceptions addressed in the preliminary plat order of decision and/or
development agreement.
   (E)   For phased developments, engineering plans should reflect the
applicable phase being developed. In the event the phase lines change, a new
set of engineering plans shall be required for each affected phase even if a
previous set has already been approved.
   (F)   The initial submittal and subsequent revision process for engineering
plans, as established by the Engineering Department, shall be followed and
shall include payment of all applicable fees.
   (G)   The approval of engineering plans by the Engineering Department is
good for one year from the date of stamped and signed approval or until the
preliminary plat expires, whichever comes first. Once engineering plans have
expired, a new set of plans will have to be submitted to the Engineering
Department for review and approval provided the preliminary plat is still
active. Review of new plans will be based upon divisions (A) through (F) above.
(Ord. 2768, passed 4-20-2009; Ord. 2811, passed 11-2-2009)
§ 11-04-04 CONSTRUCTION AND INSPECTION.
   (A)   Prior to commencement of construction of any required improvements,
construction in any dedicated right-of-way or future right-of-way area or
construction of any improvement intended for dedication to the city or
connection to a city facility, a preconstruction meeting shall be scheduled by
the engineer of record.
      (1)   Said preconstruction meeting shall take place at the Engineering
Department.
      (2)   Representatives from all applicable utilities shall be invited and
should be present.
      (3)   Applicable city personnel shall be present.
   (B)   The City Engineering Department shall be notified a minimum of two
business days in advance of all testing, including, but not limited to,
compaction, pressure and coliform testing.
      (1)   Applicable city personnel must be present at all testing or the
results will be null and void, unless applicable city personnel authorize
testing to proceed without city observation. The city shall be duly notified by
the engineer of record or his or her authorized representative a minimum of two
business days prior to the testing.
      (2)   The engineer of record or his or her designated representative must
be present at all testing or the results will be null and void.
      (3)   A log of all inspection visits and testing results shall be kept by
the engineer of record or his or her representative and a copy of said log and
testing results shall be submitted to the Engineering Department upon
completion of the improvements.
   (C)   Construction of facilities to be dedicated and/or within a public
right-of-way or future public right-of-way area shall be performed by an
appropriately licensed public works contractor and constructed to city
specifications and standards.
   (D)   The subdivider shall employ a responsible design professional,
preferably the engineer of record, to oversee and inspect construction, to
perform and/or observe all requisite testing of completed facilities and to
acknowledge in writing, that to the best of his or her knowledge, improvements
have been constructed in compliance with approved plans and city specifications
and standards.
   (E)   All public streets, public sewer lines, public water lines and water
services, up to and through the water meter, and including the water meter,
fire hydrants and streetlight facilities, shall be dedicated to the city.
   (F)   Conveyance facilities for stormwater drainage within public rights-of-
way may be eligible for dedication to the city on a case-by-case basis as
approved by the City Engineer.
   (G)   All construction staking shall be performed by or under the direct
supervision of a professional land surveyor or professional engineer and shall
be so noted on the construction plans.
   (H)   The engineer of record shall be held responsible to ensure that
required development improvements are in substantial compliance with said
engineer’s design.
(Ord. 2768, passed 4-20-2009; Ord. 2811, passed 11-2-2009)
§ 11-04-05 REQUIRED IMPROVEMENTS; STANDARDS AND SPECIFICATIONS.
   (A)   Requirements mandatory. All requirements hereinbelow, as noted in this
section, must be adhered to and no exceptions are allowed even through the
planned unit development process, unless an exception to said standards has
been granted by City Council. Any such exceptions shall be made on a case-by-
case basis only, shall not be considered precedent setting and shall be
dependent upon one or any combination of the following factors: topography;
geography; limited size of the subject property; existing site or surrounding
conditions that prohibit adherence to the requirement; whether or not the
project is an infill project; and/or whether or not the project is a
redevelopment project. In no case shall an exception be granted if, in the
opinion of City Council, said exception presents a detriment to the public’s
health, safety and/or general welfare and/or is not in the best interests of
the city. In no case shall an exception be granted if any portion of the
request for the exception is based upon financial conditions or situations. All
requested exceptions must be specifically requested and detailed in the initial
preliminary plat application and shall be considered for a recommendation by
the Commission and a final decision by the City Council.
   (B)   Adherence to various standards and specifications; streets. The
following are required improvements that shall adhere to city code, CSS, MUTCD
and the city’s transportation master plan. In certain instances, as approved by
City Council, where all buildings exist and no new construction will
immediately be taking place, curb, gutter, sidewalk, street, alley, street
lighting, approach and/or approach spacing improvements may be deferred until
such time that new construction of a primary building or unit does take place
within the subdivision/development. At the time of new construction of any
primary building or unit, all deferred improvements shall be installed as per
the standards in place at the date of submittal of the building permit
application. The Engineering Department shall not sign a certificate of
occupancy in such cases until all deferred improvements have been completed by
the applicant and inspected and accepted by the city along with applicable
record drawings, inspection logs, engineer’s certifications and dedication
requests:
      (1)   Streets and alleys;
      (2)   Curb and gutter;
      (3)   Sidewalk;
      (4)   Street name signs and other street traffic signs;
      (5)   Street lighting; and
      (6)   Construction of approach and approach spacing.
   (C)   Stormwater. Strict adherence to the “Caldwell Stormwater Management
Manual,” as adopted by City Council as well as any subsequent adopted updates,
is required.
   (D)   Sanitary sewage disposal.
      (1)   Connection to city sewer system is required.
      (2)   An individual sewage disposal service shall be installed for each
individual buildable lot.
      (3)   All sanitary sewage disposal facilities shall be designed and
subject to city code, standards, specifications and approvals and shall comply
with all applicable sewer master studies, including updates.
   (E)   Water supply.
      (1)   Connection to city water system is required. Each individual
buildable lot shall have installed an individual water service capable of
supplying each buildable lot with safe, pure and potable water in sufficient
volume flow and pressure for domestic use and fire protection in accordance
with city code, Department of Environmental Quality requirements, International
Fire Code and specifically §
08-13-01.
      (2)   All condominium units shall have individual water meters, including
existing units as well as new construction.
      (3)   Redundant water supply is required.
      (4)   All domestic services and facilities shall be designed and subject
to city code, standards, specifications and approvals and shall comply with all
applicable master water studies, including updates. Exceptions to master water
studies and master water plans may be granted by City Council.
   (F)   Irrigation. Irrigation facilities shall be provided as detailed in §
10-07-12 of the zoning regulations. The developer, subdivider and/or property
owner shall maintain any existing upstream drainage rights and downstream
irrigation rights across the subject property. The developer, subdivider,
property owner and/or engineer of record shall contact the appropriate
irrigation district to help ascertain these rights. Appropriate facilities
shall be provided by the developer, subdivider and/or property owner to convey
irrigation and drainage water across the subject property to take care of these
off-site needs. There shall be no discharge of gravity irrigation return water
into the subdivision stormwater system.
      (1)   Supplying irrigation district shall approve the location of the
point of delivery.
      (2)   Existing irrigation facilities shall be located outside the public
right-of-way and shall be moved, adjusted and/or improved as necessary to
facilitate required street improvements.
   (G)   Monuments. Monuments shall be set in accordance with Idaho Code § 50-
1303. Monuments disturbed or destroyed during construction shall be reset.
   (H)   Fire hydrants. Fire hydrants are required to meet the City Water
Department’s standards, city code standards and International Fire Code’s water
supply requirements.
      (1)   Fire hydrants shall be installed at all locations as specified in
any project plan or plat review as identified by the Fire Department.
      (2)   Fire hydrants do not need to be shown on preliminary plat maps. The
Fire Department will determine the location of all required fire hydrants
during its plan review of all preliminary plats.
      (3)   Fire hydrant locations, as determined by the Fire Department, shall
be shown on all final approved construction drawings and record drawings.
      (4)   Fire hydrants shall meet city installation standards as to the type
of hydrant and water line connections.
      (5)   Fire hydrants must be installed and operable prior to any
combustible materials being brought on the property.
      (6)   Fire hydrants shall be painted bright red, and the steamer
connection shall meet Fire Department requirements. Where subject to collision,
bollards may be required as determined and approved by the Fire Department.
   (I)   Utilities.
      (1)   The extension and relocation of power, telephone, communication,
television and similar utilities shall be at the subdivider’s expense and shall
have the capacity and placement necessary to serve land located farther out.
      (2)   Power, telephone, communication, television and similar utility
lines on the property boundary and within the subdivision shall all be
installed underground.
      (3)   When overhead distribution utility lines exist on and within the
property being platted, those lines and the new installation within the platted
area shall be underground.
      (4)   All existing and proposed easements on the subject property shall
be clearly detailed on preliminary plats, final plats, construction drawings
and record drawings with dimensions, bearings and instrument numbers.
(Ord. 2768, passed 4-20-2009; Ord. 2811, passed 11-2-2009)
§ 11-04-06 RECORD DRAWINGS.
   (A)   All record drawings shall show the following items in their respective
“as built” locations as well as showing elevations for water, sewer, storm
drainage, curb and gutter:
      (1)   Water.
         (a)   Meter placement;
         (b)   Valve placement;
         (c)   Blow off placement;
         (d)   Fire hydrant placement;
         (e)   Main lines; and
         (f)   Service lines (includes fire service lines specifically called
out).
      (2)   Sewer.
         (a)   Manhole placement;
         (b)   Cleanout placement;
         (c)   Lift station placement;
         (d)   Main lines; and
         (e)   Service lines.
      (3)   Street lighting.
         (a)   Streetlight electrical system, to include conduits, J-boxes,
power source location and pole locations; and
         (b)   Meter pedestals (if applicable).
      (4)   Pressure irrigation.
         (a)   Service placement;
         (b)   Valve placement;
         (c)   Pump out placement;
         (d)   Drain placement;
         (e)   Air vacuum placement (including air vacuum valve);
         (f)   Backflow connections;
         (g)   Pump station placement; and
         (h)   Main lines.
      (5)   Storm drain.
         (a)   Catch basin placement;
         (b)   Siphon placement;
         (c)   Manhole placement;
         (d)   Sand and grease trap placement;
         (e)   Inlet and outlet placement (ponds, seepage beds, drain ditches
and the like);
         (f)   Main lines; and
         (g)   Map SD overflow to an existing drain.
      (6)   Street signs. Placement of all street/traffic signs installed
(street name, stop, dead end and the like).
      (7)   Drawings.
         (a)   All sheets approved with the construction drawing shall be
submitted with the record drawings.
         (b)   All pages shall be “as built.”
         (c)   All pages shall be stamped and signed by the engineer of record.
         (d)   Electronic copies of the approved record drawings shall be
submitted using “.dwg” drawing file format and shall be spatially referenced to
the state plan coordinate system - west zone, North American datum (NAD) 83.
Vertical control shall be referenced to the North American vertical datum
(NAVD) 88. The unit of measurement shall be U.S. survey feet.
   (B)   Record drawings shall be submitted and approved, along with engineer
of record inspection logs and the engineer’s certification from the engineer of
record, prior to the city’s signature on the final plat unless said items are
included in the financial guarantee. Record drawings shall establish that the
engineer of record has caused construction to occur in substantial compliance
with the design of said engineer of record.
(Ord. 2768, passed 4-20-2009; Ord. 2811, passed 11-2-2009)
§ 11-04-07 FINANCIAL GUARANTEES.
   (A)   (1)   Financial guarantees shall be in the form of:
         (a)   Cash deposited with and held by the city pending final
completion of the improvements; or
         (b)   Cash backed irrevocable letter of credit, drawn from a financial
institution located within 50 miles of the city, that has been submitted to and
accepted by the City Engineer and is irrevocable until final completion of all
improvements.
      (2)   Alternate forms of financial guarantee may be accepted by the city
upon a finding by both the City Attorney and the City Engineer that such
alternate form of financial guarantee is in the best interest of the city.
   (B)   Financial guarantees shall be submitted to and accepted by the City
Engineer prior to any city signatures on the final plat.
   (C)   (1)   The developer shall provide, and be the responsible party for, a
financial guarantee as outlined within this section in an equal amount to 150%
of the itemized bids from the developer’s contractors, issued on said
contractor’s letterhead and submitted to the City Engineer for approval.
      (2)   Remaining work shall be determined by the Engineering Department,
in conjunction with the Planning and Zoning Department, in the form of a punch
list which shall be compiled by the Engineering Department following a walk-
through inspection by the Engineering Department. The punch list shall be
reviewed and accepted by both the Engineering Department and the Planning and
Zoning Department prior to issuance.
   (D)   If construction of any improvements has been deferred or postponed by
submittal of a financial guarantee, no more than 80% of the total building
permits ultimately available for the subdivision or phase for which the
financial guarantee was submitted shall be applied for by the applicant or
issued by the city.
   (E)   (1)   Regardless of the aforementioned 80% available building permits,
if construction of all improvements is not completed within 120 days following
the date of recordation of the final plat, no building permits shall be applied
for by the subdivider or issued by the city until final completion of all
improvements by the subdivider has taken place and the city has inspected and
approved all improvements.
      (2)   Provided, however, that if the failure to complete all improvements
within the 120-day period occurs through no fault of the subdivider (no fault
of the subdivider does not include economic or market conditions), the City
Engineer, at his or her sole discretion, may grant time extensions to the 120-
day period of a minimum 120 days each.
   (F)   Under no circumstances shall the city ever issue more than 80% of the
total building permits ultimately available for the subdivision or phase until
final completion of all improvements for said subdivision or phase by the
subdivider has taken place and said improvements have been inspected and
approved by the City Engineer.
   (G)   The financial guarantee is good for one year only. If construction of
improvements has not been completed within one year of submittal of the
financial guarantee, the City Engineer, at his or her sole discretion, may
grant a one-time only extension to the one-year period, said one-time only
extension not to exceed one additional year.
      (1)   The renewal amount shall be set at 175% of the City Engineer’s
estimate of cost on the remaining work.
      (2)   Estimated cost on remaining work shall be determined in part by
detailed bids from the subdivider’s contractors as issued on said contractors’
letterhead and submitted to the City Engineer.
   (H)   If construction of the improvements has not been completed within the
original one-year time period or the additional one-year time period granted by
the City Engineer through an extension, the City Engineer shall inform the
Council, through the public hearing process, at a regularly scheduled meeting.
      (1)   The Council may determine that the remaining work not completed by
the subdivider will be completed by the city and the construction costs
recovered from the financial guarantee.
      (2)   The Council may approve a second one-year time extension for
completion of the work by the subdivider.
         (a)   The renewal amount shall be set at 200% of the City Engineer’s
estimate of cost on the remaining work.
         (b)   Estimated cost on remaining work shall partially be determined
by detailed bids from the subdivider’s contractors as issued on said
contractors’ letterhead and submitted to the City Engineer.
      (3)   Further time extensions of financial guarantees beyond the second
one-year time extension are prohibited.
   (I)   Financial guarantees shall not be released by the city unless and
until all of the improvements (including required dedications) have been
completed by the subdivider and accepted by the City Engineer and by any other
applicable agencies or city departments responsible for acceptance and
maintenance.
   (J)   Financial guarantees shall be written to allow the city to draw upon
the financial guarantee at any time at the discretion of the City Engineer as
well as allowing multiple draws by the city.
(Ord. 2811, passed 11-2-2009; Ord. 3456, passed 9-1-2022; Ord. 3713, passed 10-
20-2025)
CHAPTER 5: SPECIAL SUBDIVISIONS OR PLANNED UNIT DEVELOPMENTS
